bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 【晋紀十四】起玄黓敦牂，盡昭陽協洽，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 14] From Xuanque Dunzang through Zhaoyang Xieqia; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals XIV] From the year Xuanque Dunzang through Zhaoyang Xieqia—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 中宗元皇帝下永昌元年（

translations.literal: First year of Yongchang under Emperor Yuan of the Middle Sovereign (lower scroll) (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Yongchang (lower scroll) of Emperor Yuan (

sentences.zh: 壬午，公元三二二年）

translations.literal: renwu, AD 322)
translations.idiomatic: the year Renwu, AD 322)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，郭璞複上疏，請因皇孫生，下赦令，帝從之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Guo Pu again submitted a memorial, asking that because an imperial grandson had been born an amnesty be issued; the emperor complied.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Guo Pu again memorialized the throne, urging that the birth of an imperial grandson be marked with a general amnesty; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On yimao, a great amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted a new reign title.

sentences.zh: 王敦以璞爲記室參軍。

translations.literal: Wang Dun appointed Pu recorder of the headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun made Guo Pu a recorder on his staff.

sentences.zh: 璞善卜筮，知敦必爲亂，己預其禍，甚憂之。

translations.literal: Pu was skilled in divination and knew Dun would surely rebel; he foresaw his own calamity and was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu was adept at divination and knew Wang Dun would rebel; foreseeing his own doom, he was deeply anxious.

sentences.zh: 大將軍掾穎川陳述卒，璞哭之極哀，曰：“嗣祖，焉知非福也！

translations.literal: Chen Shuzhu of Yingchuan, a clerk of the Grand General, died; Pu wept for him with extreme grief and said, "Sizu, who knows this may not be a blessing!"
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shuzhu of Yingchuan, a clerk in the Grand General's office, died, Guo Pu mourned him bitterly and said, "Sizu—who can say this is not a blessing?"

sentences.zh: 敦既與朝廷乖離，乃羈錄朝士有時望者，置己幕府，以羊曼及陳國謝鯤爲長史。

translations.literal: Dun having broken with the court, detained and enrolled court officials of reputation, placed them in his headquarters, and appointed Yang Man and Xie Kun of Chen as chief administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Dun had broken with the court, he detained eminent officials and installed them in his staff, appointing Yang Man and Xie Kun of Chen as chief administrators.

sentences.zh: 曼，祜之兄孫也。

translations.literal: Man was a grandson of Yang Hu's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Man was a grandson of Yang Hu's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 曼、鯤終日酣醉，故敦不委以事。

translations.literal: Man and Kun were drunk all day long, so Dun did not entrust them with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Man and Kun drank themselves senseless every day, so Dun never gave them real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 敦將作亂，謂鯤曰：“劉隗奸邪，將危社稷，吾欲除君側之惡，何如？

translations.literal: When Dun was about to rebel, he said to Kun, "Liu Wei is treacherous and wicked and will endanger the altars of state; I wish to remove evil at the ruler's side—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Dun prepared to rebel, he asked Xie Kun, "Liu Wei is treacherous and will endanger the realm; I mean to purge evil from the emperor's side—what say you?"

sentences.zh: ”鯤曰：“隗誠始禍，然城狐社鼠。

translations.literal: " Kun said, "Wei indeed began the trouble, yet he is a fox under the city wall and a rat at the altar—"
translations.idiomatic: " Xie Kun replied, "Liu Wei did start this trouble, but he is the court's own creature—"

sentences.zh: ”敦怒曰：“君庸才，豈達大體！

translations.literal: " Dun angrily said, "You are a mediocrity—how could you grasp the larger design!"
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dun flared up: "You are a mediocrity—what do you know of the larger design!"

sentences.zh: ”出爲豫章太守，又留不遣。

translations.literal: " He was sent out as administrator of Yuzhang but was again detained and not allowed to leave.
translations.idiomatic: " He was nominally sent out as prefect of Yuzhang, but Wang Dun kept him and would not let him go.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，敦舉兵于武昌，上疏罪狀劉隗，稱：“隗佞邪讒賊，威福自由，妄興事役，勞擾士民，賦役煩重，怨聲盈路。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Dun raised troops at Wuchang and submitted a memorial listing Liu Wei's crimes, saying, "Wei is a flatterer, wicked slanderer, and traitor who wields power and favor as he pleases, recklessly launches projects and corvée, wearies and harasses scholars and commoners, and imposes heavy taxes and labor; complaints fill the roads."
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Wang Dun raised arms at Wuchang and memorialized the throne with charges against Liu Wei: "Liu Wei is a sycophant and traitor who wields power at will, launches wasteful projects, burdens the people with heavy levies, and has filled the roads with grievances."

sentences.zh: 臣備位宰輔，不可坐視成敗，輒進軍致討。

translations.literal: Your servant holds a place among the chief ministers and cannot sit by watching success or failure; I have advanced the army to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: As one who shares in governing, I cannot sit idle while the realm's fate hangs in the balance; I have therefore marched to punish him.

sentences.zh: 隗首朝懸，諸軍夕退。

translations.literal: When Wei's head is hung at court in the morning, the armies will withdraw by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Liu Wei's head at court in the morning, and every army will stand down by evening.

sentences.zh: 昔太甲顛覆厥度，幸納伊尹之忠，殷道複昌。

translations.literal: Formerly Tai Jia overturned the norms, but fortunately accepted Yi Yin's loyalty, and the way of Yin flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Tai Jia overturned the norms of rule, yet by heeding Yi Yin's loyal counsel the house of Yin was restored.

sentences.zh: 願陛下深垂三思，則四海乂安，社稷永固矣。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty deeply ponder this thrice over, and then the four seas will be at peace and the altars of state forever secure.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will weigh this carefully, the realm will be at peace and the dynasty secure for ages.

sentences.zh: ”沈充亦起兵于吳興以應敦，敦以充爲大都督、督護東吳諸軍事。

translations.literal: " Shen Chong also raised troops at Wuxing in response to Dun; Dun made Chong grand commander and supervisor of all military affairs in eastern Wu.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Chong also took up arms in Wuxing to support Wang Dun, who appointed him grand commander with authority over all forces in eastern Wu.

sentences.zh: 敦至蕪湖，又上表罪狀刁協。

translations.literal: When Dun reached Wuhu, he again submitted a memorial listing Diao Xie's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun reached Wuhu, he submitted another memorial denouncing Diao Xie.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，乙亥，詔曰：“王敦憑恃寵靈，敢肆狂逆，方朕太甲，欲見幽囚。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered; on yihai an edict said, "Wang Dun, relying on favor and power, dares to run wild in rebellion, treating Us as Tai Jia and wishing to see Us imprisoned."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; on yihai he issued an edict: "Wang Dun, drunk on imperial favor, has dared to rebel openly, treating Us as Tai Jia and seeking to imprison Us."

sentences.zh: 是可忍也，孰不可忍！

translations.literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be borne!
translations.idiomatic: If this can be endured, what cannot?

sentences.zh: 今親帥六軍以誅大逆，有殺敦者，封五千戶侯。

translations.literal: Now We personally lead the Six Armies to punish this great traitor; whoever kills Dun shall be enfeoffed as marquis of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: We now lead the Six Armies in person to punish this arch-traitor; whoever kills Wang Dun shall receive a marquisate of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: ”敦兄光錄勛含乘輕舟逃歸于敦。

translations.literal: " Dun's elder brother Han, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, took a light boat and fled back to Dun.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dun's elder brother Han, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, fled by light boat to join his brother.

sentences.zh: 太子中庶子溫嶠謂僕射周顗曰：“大將軍此舉似有所在，當無濫邪？

translations.literal: Wen Jiao, attendant of the heir apparent, said to Zhou Yi, the vice director of the Secretariat: "The Grand General's move seems to have some purpose—surely it is not indiscriminate?"
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao, attendant to the crown prince, asked Zhou Yi, Vice Director of the Secretariat: "The Grand General's campaign seems to have a target—surely he is not striking at random?"

sentences.zh: ”顗曰：“不然。

translations.literal: " Yi said, "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Yi replied, "Not at all."

sentences.zh: 人主自非堯、舜，何能無失，人臣安可舉兵以脅之！

translations.literal: Unless the sovereign is Yao or Shun, how can he be without fault? How can a minister raise troops to coerce him!
translations.idiomatic: Unless a ruler is Yao or Shun, he will err—yet what minister may take up arms to coerce his lord!

sentences.zh: 舉動如此，豈得雲非亂乎！

translations.literal: Conduct such as this—how can one say it is not rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Conduct like this—how can anyone call it anything but rebellion!

sentences.zh: 處仲狼抗無上，其意寧有限邪！

translations.literal: Chuzhong is fierce and defiant toward his superiors—can his intent be limited!
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhong is savagely insubordinate—do you think his ambitions will stop here?

sentences.zh: 敦初起兵，遣使告梁州刺史甘卓，約與之俱下，卓許之。

translations.literal: When Dun first raised troops, he sent envoys to inform Gan Zhuo, governor of Liang Province, inviting him to march down together; Zhuo agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun first rebelled, he sent word to Gan Zhuo, governor of Liang Province, asking him to march east together; Zhuo agreed.

sentences.zh: 及敦升舟，而卓不赴，使參軍孫雙詣武昌諫止敦。

translations.literal: When Dun boarded his ships, Zhuo did not come; he sent his staff officer Sun Shuang to Wuchang to remonstrate and stop Dun.
translations.idiomatic: But when Wang Dun embarked, Zhuo did not follow; instead he sent his aide Sun Shuang to Wuchang to urge him to turn back.

sentences.zh: 敦驚曰：“甘侯前與吾語雲何，而更有异？

translations.literal: Dun said in alarm, "What did Lord Gan say to me before, that he now has a different view?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun exclaimed in alarm, "What did Lord Gan tell me before—and now he changes his mind?"

sentences.zh: 正當慮吾危朝廷耳！

translations.literal: He must be worrying that I endanger the court!
translations.idiomatic: He must fear that I threaten the court!

sentences.zh: 吾今但除奸凶，若事濟，當以甘侯作公。

translations.literal: I now only remove traitors and villains; if the affair succeeds, I shall make Lord Gan a duke.
translations.idiomatic: I am only rooting out traitors; if we succeed, I will make Lord Gan a duke.

sentences.zh: ”雙還報，卓意狐疑。

translations.literal: " Shuang returned with his report, and Zhuo's mind was divided.
translations.idiomatic: " When Sun Shuang returned, Zhuo was torn with doubt.

sentences.zh: 或說卓：“且僞許敦，待敦至都而討之。

translations.literal: Someone urged Zhuo, "For now falsely agree with Dun and wait until he reaches the capital to punish him."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Zhuo, "Pretend to agree with Wang Dun for now, then strike when he reaches the capital."

sentences.zh: ”卓曰：“昔陳敏之亂，吾先從而後圖之，論者謂吾懼逼而思變，心常愧之。

translations.literal: " Zhuo said, "In Chen Min's rebellion I first followed and only afterward plotted; critics said I feared coercion and then changed sides, and I have always felt ashamed in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuo said, "When Chen Min rebelled, I sided with him first and turned only later; people said I bowed to force and then switched—I've never lived that down."

sentences.zh: 今若複爾，何以自明！

translations.literal: If I do the same again now, how can I clear myself!
translations.idiomatic: If I do that again, how can I ever justify myself!

sentences.zh: ”卓使人以敦旨告順陽太守魏該，該曰：“我所以起兵拒胡賊者，正欲忠于王室耳。

translations.literal: " Zhuo sent someone to convey Dun's orders to Wei Gai, administrator of Shunyang; Gai said, "The reason I raised troops to resist the barbarian invaders was precisely to be loyal to the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuo sent a messenger with Wang Dun's orders to Wei Gai, prefect of Shunyang. Gai replied, "I took up arms against the barbarians to serve the throne."

sentences.zh: 今王公舉兵向天子，非吾所宜與也。

translations.literal: Now the prince and lord raise troops against the Son of Heaven—this is not something I should join.
translations.idiomatic: Now a prince marches against the Son of Heaven—that is not a cause I can join.

sentences.zh: ”遂絕之。

translations.literal: " He broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: " He broke with them entirely.

sentences.zh: 敦遣參軍桓羆說譙王承，請承爲軍司。

translations.literal: Dun sent his staff officer Huan Pi to persuade Prince of Qiao Cheng, asking Cheng to serve as army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun sent his aide Huan Pi to win over Prince of Qiao Sima Cheng, offering him the post of army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 承嘆曰：“吾其死矣！

translations.literal: Cheng sighed and said, "I am as good as dead!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sighed, "I am as good as dead!"

sentences.zh: 地荒民寡，勢孤援絕，將何以濟！

translations.literal: The land is desolate, the people few, my position isolated and aid cut off—how can I succeed!
translations.idiomatic: The land is barren, the people few, I stand alone without allies—how can I prevail!

sentences.zh: 然得死忠義，夫複何求！

translations.literal: Yet if I can die in loyalty and righteousness, what more is there to seek!
translations.idiomatic: Yet if I may die loyal and righteous, what more could I ask!

sentences.zh: ”承檄長沙虞悝爲長史，會悝遭母喪，承往吊之，曰：“吾欲討王敦，而兵少糧乏，且新到，恩信未洽。

translations.literal: " Cheng summoned Yu Ti of Changsha as chief administrator; it happened that Ti was in mourning for his mother, and Cheng went to offer condolences, saying, "I wish to campaign against Wang Dun, but troops are few and grain scarce, and having only recently arrived, favor and trust are not yet established."
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng summoned Yu Ti of Changsha as his chief administrator. Ti was in mourning for his mother, and Cheng went to condole with him, saying, "I mean to strike Wang Dun, but my forces are few, supplies thin, and as a newcomer I have not yet won the people's trust."

sentences.zh: 卿兄弟，湘中之豪俊，王室方危，金革之事，古人所不辭，將何以教之？

translations.literal: You and your brothers are eminent men of central Xiang; the royal house is in peril; affairs of arms are what the ancients did not refuse—what will you teach me?"
translations.idiomatic: You and your brothers are the leading men of the Xiang region; the throne is in peril; the ancients did not shrink from war—what counsel have you for me?"

sentences.zh: ”悝曰：“大王不以悝兄弟猥劣，親屈臨之，敢不致死！

translations.literal: " Ti said, "Your Highness, not deeming me and my brothers base and inferior, has personally stooped to visit us—we dare not fail to give our lives!"
translations.idiomatic: " Ti replied, "Your Highness honors us despite our low station by coming in person—we dare not hold back our lives!"

sentences.zh: 然鄙州荒弊，難以進討；

translations.literal: Yet our humble province is desolate and impoverished, and it is hard to advance in attack;
translations.idiomatic: Yet our province is poor and weak, and a direct advance is hard;

sentences.zh: 宜且收衆固守，傳檄四方，敦勢必分，分而圖之，庶幾可捷也。

translations.literal: it would be better first to gather troops and hold firm, send proclamations to the four quarters—Dun's strength will surely be divided, and by dividing and then plotting against him, we may perhaps gain victory.
translations.idiomatic: better to gather your forces, hold fast, and issue proclamations everywhere—Wang Dun's power will split, and once divided he can be overcome.

sentences.zh: ”承乃囚桓羆，以悝爲長史，以其弟望爲司馬，督護諸軍，與零陵太守尹奉、建昌太守長沙王循、衡陽太守淮陵劉翼、舂陵令長沙易雄，同舉兵討敦。

translations.literal: " Cheng then imprisoned Huan Pi, made Ti chief administrator, and appointed Ti's younger brother Wang as marshal to supervise all armies; together with Yin Feng, administrator of Lingling, Wang Xun of Changsha, administrator of Jianchang, Liu Yi of Huailing, administrator of Hengyang, and Yi Xiong of Changsha, magistrate of Chunling, he jointly raised troops to punish Dun.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng imprisoned Huan Pi, made Yu Ti his chief administrator and Ti's brother Wang marshal over all forces, and together with Yin Feng of Lingling, Wang Xun of Jianchang, Liu Yi of Hengyang, and Yi Xiong of Chunling, raised arms against Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 雄移檄遠近，列敦罪惡，于是一州之內皆應承。

translations.literal: Xiong sent proclamations near and far listing Dun's crimes, and within the province all responded to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Xiong circulated proclamations far and wide listing Wang Dun's crimes, and the whole province rallied to Cheng.

sentences.zh: 惟湘東太守鄭淡不從，承使虞望討斬之，以徇四境。

translations.literal: Only Zheng Dan, administrator of Xiangdong, did not follow; Cheng sent Yu Wang to campaign against and behead him, displaying the head to the four borders.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zheng Dan, prefect of eastern Xiang, refused; Cheng sent Yu Wang to execute him and display the head throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 淡，敦姊夫也。

translations.literal: Dan was Dun's brother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Dan was Wang Dun's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 承遣主簿鄧騫至襄陽，說甘卓曰：“劉大連雖驕蹇失衆心，非有害于天下。

translations.literal: Cheng sent his chief clerk Deng Qian to Xiangyang to persuade Gan Zhuo, saying, "Liu Dalian, though arrogant and harsh and having lost popular support, has not harmed the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sent his chief clerk Deng Qian to Xiangyang to urge Gan Zhuo: "Liu Wei may be arrogant and unpopular, but he has not harmed the realm."

sentences.zh: 大將軍以其私憾，稱兵向闕，此忠臣義士竭節之時也。

translations.literal: The Grand General, from private resentment, has raised troops toward the palace—this is the hour for loyal ministers and righteous men to exhaust their devotion.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General marches on the capital from private spite—this is the hour for loyal men to give their all.

sentences.zh: 公受任方伯，奉辭伐罪，乃桓、文之功也。

translations.literal: Your Lordship holds a regional command and bears the mandate to punish crime—this is the achievement of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: You hold a regional command and the mandate to punish rebels—this is the achievement of a Duke Huan or Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: ”卓曰：“桓、文則非吾所能，然志在徇國，當共詳思之。

translations.literal: " Zhuo said, "Duke Huan and Duke Wen are beyond my capacity, yet my will is to give my life for the state—we should deliberate together in detail."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuo replied, "I am no Duke Huan or Duke Wen, but my heart is for the realm—we must think this through together."

sentences.zh: ”參軍李梁說卓曰：“昔隗囂跋扈，竇融保河西以奉光武，卒受其福。

translations.literal: " The staff officer Li Liang urged Zhuo, saying, "Formerly Wei Xiao was overbearing; Dou Rong held Hexi to serve Emperor Guangwu and in the end received his reward."
translations.idiomatic: " Staff officer Li Liang urged Zhuo: "When Wei Xiao grew overbearing, Dou Rong held Hexi for Emperor Guangwu and was richly rewarded in the end."

sentences.zh: 今將軍有重望于天下，但當按兵坐以待之，使大將軍事捷，當委將軍以方面，不捷，朝廷必以將軍代之。

translations.literal: Now the general has great standing in the realm; you need only hold your troops and sit waiting. If the Grand General succeeds, he will entrust you with a frontier region; if he fails, the court will surely replace him with you.
translations.idiomatic: You enjoy great prestige today—hold your army and wait. If the Grand General wins, he will give you a frontier command; if he loses, the court will put you in his place.

sentences.zh: 何憂不富貴，而釋此廟勝，决存亡于一戰邪？

translations.literal: Why worry about not gaining wealth and rank, yet abandon this victory decided at the temple and stake survival on a single battle?"
translations.idiomatic: Why abandon a winning strategy assured in council and stake everything on one battle?"

sentences.zh: ”騫謂梁曰：“光武當創業之初，故隗、竇可以文服從容顧望。

translations.literal: " Qian said to Liang, "When Guangwu was at the start of founding his enterprise, Wei and Dou could with civil rites wait at ease and look about."
translations.idiomatic: " Qian told Liang, "Guangwu was still founding his dynasty—that is why Wei Xiao and Dou Rong could wait and watch."

sentences.zh: 今將軍之于本朝，非竇融之比也；

translations.literal: The general's relation to this dynasty is not comparable to Dou Rong;
translations.idiomatic: You are no Dou Rong to this court;

sentences.zh: 襄陽之于太府，非河西之固也。

translations.literal: and Xiangyang's relation to the imperial capital is not the solidity of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: and Xiangyang is not the impregnable Hexi of old.

sentences.zh: 使大將軍克劉隗，還武昌，增石城之戍，絕荊、湘之粟，將軍欲安歸乎！

translations.literal: If the Grand General defeats Liu Wei, returns to Wuchang, increases the garrison at Stone City, and cuts off grain from Jing and Xiang—where will the general wish to return in peace!
translations.idiomatic: If the Grand General defeats Liu Wei, returns to Wuchang, reinforces Stone City, and cuts off grain from Jing and Xiang—where will you go then!

sentences.zh: 勢在人手，而曰我處廟勝，未之聞也。

translations.literal: The advantage is in another's hands, yet you say you sit in temple victory—I have never heard of such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: The advantage lies with another, yet you speak of assured victory in council—I have never heard the like.

sentences.zh: 且爲人臣，國家有難，坐視不救，于義安乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, as a minister, when the state is in difficulty, to sit and watch without rescue—how is that righteous!
translations.idiomatic: And as a minister, when the state is in peril, to sit idle—where is the righteousness in that!

sentences.zh: ”卓尚疑之。

translations.literal: " Zhuo still hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuo still wavered.

sentences.zh: 騫曰：“今既不爲義舉，又不承大將軍檄，此必至之禍，愚智所見也。

translations.literal: Qian said, "Now, neither making a righteous move nor accepting the Grand General's summons—this is disaster that must come, plain to fool and sage alike."
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "If you neither act for righteousness nor answer the Grand General's summons, disaster is certain—any fool can see it."

sentences.zh: 且議者之所難，以彼强而我弱也。

translations.literal: Moreover, what debaters find difficult is that they are strong and we are weak.
translations.idiomatic: What troubles your advisers is that he seems strong and you weak.

sentences.zh: 今大將軍兵不過萬餘，其留者不能五千；

translations.literal: Now the Grand General's troops do not exceed ten thousand-odd, and those left behind cannot reach five thousand;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General has barely ten thousand men, and fewer than five thousand remain behind;

sentences.zh: 而將軍見衆既倍之矣。

translations.literal: while the general's visible forces already double them.
translations.idiomatic: while the forces you can field already double his.

sentences.zh: 以將軍之威名，帥此府之精銳，杖節鳴鼓，以順討逆，豈王含所能禦哉！

translations.literal: With the general's prestige, leading this province's elite troops, bearing the staff and beating the drums to punish the rebel in the name of righteousness—how could Wang Han withstand it!
translations.idiomatic: With your renown, leading this province's best troops under imperial authority to punish rebellion—how could Wang Han stand against you!

sentences.zh: 溯流之衆，勢不自救，將軍之舉武昌，若摧枯拉朽，尚何顧慮邪！

translations.literal: The forces rowing upstream cannot save themselves; the general's strike at Wuchang would be like snapping dry wood—what need for hesitation!
translations.idiomatic: His upstream army cannot save itself; your strike at Wuchang would shatter it like rotten timber—what is there to fear!

sentences.zh: 武昌既定，據其軍實，鎮撫二州，以恩意招懷士卒，使還者如歸，此呂蒙所以克關羽也。

translations.literal: Once Wuchang is secured, seize its military stores, pacify the two provinces, and with kindness win over the soldiers so that those who return feel as if coming home—this is how Lü Meng overcame Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Take Wuchang, seize his supplies, pacify the two provinces, and win his soldiers with kindness so they return as to home—that is how Lü Meng defeated Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 今釋必勝之策，安坐以待危亡，不可以言智矣。

translations.literal: Now to abandon a strategy of certain victory and sit at ease awaiting peril and ruin—one cannot call that wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon a winning plan and sit idle awaiting ruin cannot be called wisdom.

sentences.zh: 敦恐卓于後爲變，又遣參軍丹楊樂道融往邀之，必欲與之俱東。

translations.literal: Dun feared Zhuo would turn against him afterward and again sent his staff officer Yue Daorong of Danyang to invite him, insisting that he march east together.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Gan Zhuo might turn on him later, Wang Dun sent his aide Yue Daorong of Danyang to press him to march east together.

sentences.zh: 道融雖事敦，而忿其悖逆，乃說卓曰：“主上親臨萬機，自用譙王爲湘州，非專任劉隗也。

translations.literal: Daorong, though serving Dun, resented his rebellion and therefore urged Zhuo, saying, "The sovereign personally handles the myriad affairs of state; he himself appointed the Prince of Qiao to Xiang Province—it is not exclusive reliance on Liu Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Though Daorong served Wang Dun, he hated the rebellion and urged Zhuo: "The emperor governs in person; he appointed the Prince of Qiao to Hunan himself—he does not rely solely on Liu Wei."

sentences.zh: 而王氏擅權日久，卒見分政，便謂失職，背恩肆逆，舉兵向闕。

translations.literal: Yet the Wang clan has monopolized power for long; when they finally saw government divided, they deemed it loss of office, turned their backs on grace and ran wild in rebellion, and raised troops toward the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang clan has held power for years; when they saw authority shared, they called it loss of office, betrayed the throne, and marched on the capital.

sentences.zh: 國家遇君至厚，今與之同，豈不違負大義！

translations.literal: The state has treated you with utmost generosity; to join them now—does that not violate great righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: The state has treated you generously—will you join them and betray that trust!

sentences.zh: 生爲逆臣，死爲愚鬼，永爲宗黨之耻，不亦惜乎！

translations.literal: Alive you would be a rebellious minister, dead a foolish ghost, forever the shame of your clan—is that not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Alive a traitor, dead a fool, forever a disgrace to your clan—is that not a waste!

sentences.zh: 爲君之計，莫若僞許應命，而馳襲武昌，大將軍士衆聞之，必不戰自潰，大勛可就矣。

translations.literal: For your plan, nothing is better than falsely agreeing to the command while galloping to strike Wuchang; when the Grand General's soldiers hear of it, they will surely collapse without fighting, and great merit can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Your best course is to pretend to agree, then strike Wuchang at speed; when Wang Dun's troops hear of it, they will scatter without a fight, and your glory will be won.

sentences.zh: ”卓雅不欲從敦，聞道融之言，遂决，曰：“吾本意也。

translations.literal: " Zhuo had always been unwilling to follow Dun; hearing Daorong's words, he resolved himself and said, "That has always been my intent."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuo had never wanted to follow Wang Dun; hearing Daorong, he made up his mind: "That has always been my intent."

sentences.zh: ”乃與巴東監軍柳純、南平太守夏侯承、宜都太守譚該等露檄數敦逆狀，帥所統致討。

translations.literal: " He then joined with Liu Chun, overseer of Badong, Xiahou Cheng, administrator of Nanping, Tan Gai, administrator of Yidu, and others in an open proclamation listing Dun's rebellious acts, and led the forces under his command to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: " He joined Liu Chun of Badong, Xiahou Cheng of Nanping, Tan Gai of Yidu, and others in a public proclamation listing Wang Dun's crimes, and led his forces against him.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍司馬贊、孫雙奉表詣台，羅英至廣州約陶侃同進。

translations.literal: He sent his staff officers Sima Zan and Sun Shuang to present a memorial at court, and Luo Ying to Guangzhou to arrange a joint advance with Tao Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Sima Zan and Sun Shuang with a memorial to court, and Luo Ying to Guangzhou to coordinate with Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 戴淵在江西，先得卓書，表上之，台內皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Dai Yuan was west of the river and first received Zhuo's letter; he memorialized it upward, and within the court all cried "Long live [the emperor]!"
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yuan west of the river received Zhuo's letter first and forwarded it to court; the whole capital erupted in cheers.

sentences.zh: 陶侃得卓信，即遣參軍高寶帥兵北下。

translations.literal: Tao Kan received Zhuo's message and at once sent his staff officer Gao Bao to lead troops north.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan received the news and immediately sent Gao Bao north with his troops.

sentences.zh: 武昌城中傳卓軍至，人皆奔散。

translations.literal: In Wuchang city it was rumored that Zhuo's army had arrived, and everyone fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread in Wuchang that Gan Zhuo's army was coming, the city emptied in panic.

sentences.zh: 敦遣從母弟南蠻校尉魏乂、將軍李恒帥甲卒二萬攻長沙。

translations.literal: Dun sent his younger cousin by a different mother, Wei Yi, colonel of the Southern Man, and the general Li Heng to lead twenty thousand armored soldiers to attack Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun sent his cousin Wei Yi, colonel of the Southern Man, and General Li Heng with twenty thousand men to attack Changsha.

sentences.zh: 長沙城池不完，資儲又闕，人情震恐。

translations.literal: Changsha's walls and moat were incomplete, stores were lacking, and popular sentiment was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha's walls were unfinished, supplies scarce, and the people were terrified.

sentences.zh: 或說譙王承，南投陶侃或退據零、桂。

translations.literal: Someone urged Prince of Qiao Cheng to flee south to Tao Kan or withdraw and hold Ling and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Prince of Qiao Cheng to flee south to Tao Kan or fall back to Ling and Gui.

sentences.zh: 承曰：“吾之起兵，志欲死于忠義，豈可貪生苟免，爲奔敗之將乎！

translations.literal: Cheng said, "I raised troops intending to die in loyalty and righteousness—how could I cling to life and seek escape, becoming a fleeing, defeated commander!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "I took up arms to die loyal—how could I cling to life and flee like a beaten general!"

sentences.zh: 事之不濟，令百姓知吾心耳。

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, let the common people know my heart—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, let the people at least know my heart.

sentences.zh: ”乃嬰城固守。

translations.literal: " He then closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: " He closed the city and held his ground.

sentences.zh: 未幾，虞望戰死，甘卓欲留鄧騫爲參軍，騫不可。

translations.literal: Before long, Yu Wang died in battle; Gan Zhuo wished to retain Deng Qian as staff officer, but Qian would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu Wang fell in battle; Gan Zhuo tried to keep Deng Qian on his staff, but Qian refused.

sentences.zh: 卓乃遣參軍虞沖與騫偕至長沙，遺譙王承書，勸之固守，當以兵出沔口，斷敦歸路，則湘圍自解。

translations.literal: Zhuo then sent his staff officer Yu Chong together with Qian to Changsha, forwarding a letter to Prince of Qiao Cheng, urging him to hold firm: troops should be sent out at Mian mouth to cut off Dun's return route, and the siege of Hunan would resolve itself.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo sent Yu Chong and Deng Qian to Changsha with a letter to Prince of Qiao Cheng, urging him to hold the city and march to Mian mouth to cut Wang Dun's retreat—then the siege would lift on its own.

sentences.zh: 承複書稱：“江左中興，草創始爾，豈圖惡逆萌自寵臣！

translations.literal: Cheng replied in a letter, saying, "The restoration east of the Yangtze has only just begun its founding—who could have imagined that wicked treachery would spring from a favored minister!
translations.idiomatic: Cheng wrote back: "The restoration south of the Yangtze has barely begun—who dreamed treason would sprout from a court favorite!

sentences.zh: 吾以宗室受任，志在隕命；

translations.literal: I received appointment as a member of the imperial clan; my will is to perish in the line of duty;
translations.idiomatic: As a prince of the blood I took this post intending to die for the throne;

sentences.zh: 而至止尚淺，凡百茫然。

translations.literal: yet my time here is still short, and in every matter I am at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: but I have only just arrived, and in every matter I am at a loss.

sentences.zh: 足下能卷甲電赴，猶有所及；

translations.literal: If you below can roll up your armor and come like lightning, something may still be achieved;
translations.idiomatic: If you can march at once with all speed, there is still time;

sentences.zh: 若其狐疑，則求我于枯魚之肆矣。

translations.literal: if you hesitate, you will seek me in the dried-fish market."
translations.idiomatic: if you waver, you will look for me among the dried fish—too late."

sentences.zh: ”卓不能從。

translations.literal: Zhuo could not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo would not act on it.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲午，封皇子昱爲琅邪王。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiawu, the prince Yu was enfeoffed as Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day jiawu, Prince Yu was enfeoffed as Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒立子弘爲世子。

translations.literal: The Later Zhao king Shi Le installed his son Hong as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's King Shi Le named his son Hong heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 遣中山公虎將精卒四萬擊徐龕。

translations.literal: He sent the Duke of Zhongshan Shi Hu to lead forty thousand elite troops to attack Xu Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shi Hu, Duke of Zhongshan, with forty thousand picked troops against Xu Kan.

sentences.zh: 龕堅守不戰，虎築長圍守之。

translations.literal: Kan held firm and would not give battle; Hu built a long encirclement to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Kan shut himself in and refused to fight; Hu threw a tight cordon around the city.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜自將擊楊難敵，難敵逆戰，不勝，退保仇池。

translations.literal: The Zhao ruler Liu Yao personally led troops to attack Yang Nandei; Nandei met them in battle, was defeated, and withdrew to defend Qiu Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's Liu Yao marched in person against Yang Nandei; Nandei gave battle, lost, and fell back on Qiu Chi.

sentences.zh: 仇池諸氐、羌及故晋王保將楊韜、隴西太守梁勛皆降于曜。

translations.literal: The Di and Qiang of Qiu Chi, Yang Tao general of the former Jin king Yang Bao, and Liangxi governor Liang Xun all surrendered to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang around Qiu Chi, Yang Bao's general Yang Tao, and Liangxi governor Liang Xun all submitted to Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 曜遷隴西萬餘戶于長安，進攻仇池。

translations.literal: Yao moved more than ten thousand households from Longxi to Chang'an and advanced to attack Qiu Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao resettled over ten thousand Longxi households in Chang'an and pressed the attack on Qiu Chi.

sentences.zh: 會軍中大疫，曜亦得疾，將引兵還；

translations.literal: Just then a great plague broke out in the army, and Yao also fell ill; he was about to lead the army back;
translations.idiomatic: A plague swept the camp and Yao himself fell ill; he prepared to withdraw;

sentences.zh: 恐難敵躡其後，乃遣光國中郎將王獷說難敵，諭以禍福，難敵遣使稱籓。

translations.literal: fearing Nandei would follow in pursuit, he sent the Palace Attendant Wang Du to persuade Nandei, explaining fortune and calamity; Nandei sent envoys to declare himself a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: fearing pursuit, he sent Wang Du to reason with Nandei on gain and loss; Nandei sent envoys to swear fealty.

sentences.zh: 曜以難敵爲假黃鉞，都督益、寧、南秦、凉、梁、巴六州、隴上、西域諸軍事，上大將軍、益、寧、南秦三州牧、武都王。

translations.literal: Yao made Nandei acting holder of the yellow battle-axe, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the six provinces of Yi, Ning, Southern Qin, Liang, Liang, and Ba, Longshang, and the Western Regions, Grand General, governor of the three provinces of Yi, Ning, and Southern Qin, and Prince of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao invested him with the yellow battle-axe, command over six provinces plus Longshang and the Western Regions, the rank of Grand General, governorship of Yi, Ning, and Southern Qin, and the title Prince of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史陳安求朝于曜，曜辭以疾。

translations.literal: Qin Province governor Chen An requested audience with Yao; Yao declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou governor Chen An asked to attend court; Yao refused, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 安怒，以爲曜已卒，大掠而歸。

translations.literal: An grew angry, believing Yao had already died, and plundered extensively on his return.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, An assumed Yao was dead and looted his way home.

sentences.zh: 曜疾甚，乘馬輿而還。

translations.literal: Yao's illness was severe; he returned in a horse-drawn litter.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was gravely ill and rode back in a litter.

sentences.zh: 使其將呼延實監輜重于後，安邀擊，獲之，謂實曰：“劉曜已死，子尚誰佐！

translations.literal: He had his general Huyan Shi guard the baggage train in the rear; An ambushed and captured him, saying to Shi, "Liu Yao is already dead—whom would you still serve!
translations.idiomatic: He left Huyan Shi with the baggage train; Chen An ambushed and seized him, saying, "Liu Yao is dead—whom will you serve now?

sentences.zh: 吾當與子共定大業。

translations.literal: I shall accomplish the great enterprise together with you.
translations.idiomatic: Join me and we will settle the realm together.

sentences.zh: ”寔叱之曰：“汝受人寵祿而叛之，自視智能何如主上？

translations.literal: Shi rebuked him, saying, "You received favor and salary from your lord yet rebel—what do you think your talent and wisdom are compared to your sovereign's?
translations.idiomatic: Shi thundered back: "You ate your lord's bread and turned traitor—do you fancy yourself his equal?

sentences.zh: 吾見汝不日梟首于上邽市，何謂大業！

translations.literal: I foresee your head on a spike in Shanggui market before many days—what great enterprise is that!
translations.idiomatic: I see your head on the Shanggui gibbet within days—what "great enterprise" is that!

sentences.zh: 宜速殺我！

translations.literal: Kill me quickly!
translations.idiomatic: Kill me now!

sentences.zh: ”安怒，殺之，以實長史魯憑爲參軍。

translations.literal: An grew angry and killed him, appointing Shi's chief clerk Lu Ping as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, An had him executed and took Shi's chief clerk Lu Ping onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 安遣其弟集帥騎三萬追曜，衛將軍呼延瑜逆擊，斬之。

translations.literal: An sent his younger brother Ji with thirty thousand cavalry to pursue Yao; Defender-in-Chief Huyan Yu met them in a counterattack and beheaded Ji.
translations.idiomatic: An sent his brother Ji with thirty thousand horse to run Yao down; Huyan Yu counterattacked and killed Ji.

sentences.zh: 安乃還上邽，遣將襲汧城，拔之。

translations.literal: An then returned to Shanggui and sent generals to raid Qian city and capture it.
translations.idiomatic: An withdrew to Shanggui and sent troops to storm Qian city and take it.

sentences.zh: 隴上氐、羌皆附于安，有衆十餘萬，自稱大都督、假黃鉞、大將軍、雍、凉、秦、梁四州牧、凉王，以趙募爲相國。

translations.literal: The Di and Qiang of Longshang all attached themselves to An, numbering more than a hundred thousand; he styled himself Grand Commander, acting holder of the yellow battle-axe, Grand General, governor of the four provinces of Yong, Liang, Qin, and Liang, and King of Liang, appointing Zhao Mu as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang of Longshang rallied to him—over a hundred thousand strong—and he proclaimed himself Grand Commander, King of Liang, and governor of four provinces, with Zhao Mu as his chancellor.

sentences.zh: 魯憑對安大哭曰：“吾不忍見陳安之死也！

translations.literal: Lu Ping wept loudly before An, saying, "I cannot bear to see Chen An die!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ping wailed before Chen An: "I cannot bear to watch you die!

sentences.zh: ”安怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: An grew angry and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, An ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 憑曰：“死自吾分，懸吾頭于上邽市，觀趙之斬陳安也！

translations.literal: Ping said, "Death is my allotted share—hang my head in Shanggui market and watch Zhao behead Chen An!
translations.idiomatic: Ping said, "Death is mine by right—hang my head in Shanggui market and watch Zhao behead Chen An!

sentences.zh: ”遂殺之。

translations.literal: They killed him.
translations.idiomatic: And they killed him.

sentences.zh: 曜聞之，慟哭曰：“賢人，民之望也。

translations.literal: When Yao heard, he wept in grief, saying, "A worthy man is the people's hope.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao heard, he mourned aloud: "A worthy man is what the people look to.

sentences.zh: 陳安于求賢之秋而多殺賢者，吾知其無所爲也！

translations.literal: Chen An, in the season of seeking worthies, kills many worthies—I know he will accomplish nothing!
translations.idiomatic: Chen An slaughters the very men he should be gathering—in the season of seeking talent he murders the talented. He will come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 休屠王石武以桑城降趙，趙以武爲秦州刺史，封酒泉王。

translations.literal: The Xiutu king Shi Wu surrendered Sang city to Zhao; Zhao made Wu governor of Qin Province and enfeoffed him as Prince of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiutu king Shi Wu surrendered Sang city to Zhao; Zhao made him governor of Qinzhou and Prince of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 帝征戴淵、劉隗入衛建康。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Dai Yuan and Liu Wei to enter and guard Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Dai Yuan and Liu Wei to defend Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 隗至，百官迎于道，隗岸幘大言，意氣自若。

translations.literal: When Wei arrived, officials welcomed him on the road; Wei wore his cap back and spoke loudly, utterly self-assured.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wei arrived, officials lined the road to greet him; he wore his cap rakishly and boomed his replies, utterly at ease.

sentences.zh: 及入見，與刁協勸帝盡誅王氏；

translations.literal: On entering audience, he and Diao Xie urged the emperor to execute the entire Wang clan;
translations.idiomatic: At audience he and Diao Xie urged the emperor to exterminate the whole Wang clan;

sentences.zh: 帝不許，隗始有懼色。

translations.literal: the emperor refused; Wei began to show fear.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused—and Wei turned pale.

sentences.zh: 司空導帥其從弟中領軍邃、左衛將軍廙、侍中侃、彬及諸宗族二十餘人，每旦詣台待罪。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Works Wang Dao led his cousins Central Army Commander Xun, Left Guard General Kuang, Palace Attendant Dan and Bin, and more than twenty clansmen—each morning they went to the court compound to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao, Supervisor of Works, led his cousins Wang Xun, Wang Kuang, Wang Dan, Wang Bin, and more than twenty kinsmen to the palace gate each dawn to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 周顗將入，導呼之曰：“伯仁，以百口累卿！

translations.literal: Zhou Yi was about to enter; Dao called to him, saying, "Boren, I entrust a hundred lives to you!
translations.idiomatic: As Zhou Yi was about to enter, Dao called after him: "Boren—I am staking a hundred lives on you!

sentences.zh: ”顗直入不顧。

translations.literal: Yi went straight in without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: Yi walked straight in without a glance back.

sentences.zh: 既見帝，言導忠誠，申救甚至；

translations.literal: Having seen the emperor, he spoke of Dao's loyalty and pleaded for him at utmost length;
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor he testified to Dao's loyalty and pleaded for his life at greatest length;

sentences.zh: 帝納其言。

translations.literal: the emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor was persuaded.

sentences.zh: 顗喜飲酒，至醉而出，導猶在門，又呼之。

translations.literal: Yi loved wine; drunk he came out; Dao was still at the gate and called to him again.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was fond of wine and came out drunk; Dao was still at the gate and called to him again.

sentences.zh: 顗不與言，顧左右曰：“今年殺諸賊奴，取金印如鬥大，系肘後。

translations.literal: Yi did not speak to him but said to those beside him, "This year I'll kill those rebel slaves and get a seal big as a dipper to hang behind my elbow.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ignored him and told his attendants, "This year we'll cut down those rebel wretches and I'll wear a seal as big as a dipper on my arm.

sentences.zh: ”既出，又上表明導無罪，言甚切至。

translations.literal: After leaving he also submitted a memorial declaring Dao innocent, expressed with utmost urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Once outside he also memorialized the throne declaring Dao innocent, in the most urgent terms.

sentences.zh: 導不之知，甚恨之。

translations.literal: Dao did not know this and hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Dao knew nothing of this and hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 帝命還導朝服，召見之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Dao's court robes restored and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor restored Dao's court dress and summoned him.

sentences.zh: 導稽首曰：“逆臣賊子，何代無之，不意今者近出臣族！

translations.literal: Dao kowtowed, saying, "Rebellious ministers and wicked sons appear in every age—I never thought they would emerge so close in my own clan!
translations.idiomatic: Dao kowtowed and said, "Traitors arise in every age—but I never dreamed one would spring from my own house!

sentences.zh: ”帝跣而執其手曰：“茂弘，方寄卿以百里之命，是何言邪！

translations.literal: The emperor went barefoot and took his hand, saying, "Maohong, I am entrusting you with authority over a hundred li of realm—what words are these!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went barefoot to take his hand: "Maohong, I am entrusting the fate of the realm to you—what talk is this!

sentences.zh: 三月，以導爲前鋒大都督，加戴淵驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, Dao was made Grand Vanguard Commander; Dai Yuan was promoted to Flying Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Wang Dao was named Grand Vanguard Commander and Dai Yuan was made Flying Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：“導以大義滅親，可以吾爲安東時節假之。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Dao, putting righteousness above kin, may have authority as when I was Pacifier of the East."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Dao has put duty above blood—grant him the same powers I held as Pacifier of the East."

sentences.zh: ”以周顗爲尚書左僕射，王邃爲右僕射。

translations.literal: Zhou Yi was made Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat; Wang Xun Vice Director of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Wang Xun Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 帝遣王廙往諭止敦；

translations.literal: The emperor sent Wang Kuang to go announce and urge Dun to stop;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wang Kuang to bid Wang Dun halt;

sentences.zh: 敦不從而留之，廙更爲敦用。

translations.literal: Dun would not obey but detained him; Kuang thereafter served Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Dun refused and kept him; Kuang then went over to Dun's side.

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍周札，素矜險好利，帝以爲右將軍、都督石頭諸軍事。

translations.literal: General Who Suppresses the Barbarians Zhou Zha, who prided himself on dangerous schemes and loved profit, was made Right General and commander of Stone City forces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zha, General Who Suppresses the Barbarians—a man proud of his cunning and greedy for gain—was made Right General and commander at Stone City.

sentences.zh: 敦將至，帝使劉隗軍金城，札守石頭，帝親被甲徇師于郊外。

translations.literal: As Dun was about to arrive, the emperor sent Liu Wei's army to Jincheng and Zha to guard Stone City; the emperor personally donned armor and reviewed troops outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Dun approached, the emperor posted Liu Wei at Jincheng and Zhou Zha at Stone City, then donned armor himself and reviewed the troops outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 以甘卓爲鎮南大將軍、侍中、都督荊、梁二州諸軍事，陶侃領江州刺史；

translations.literal: Gan Zhuo was made Grand General Who Guards the South, attendant, commander of military affairs in Jing and Liang provinces; Tao Kan took charge of Jiang Province;
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo was named Grand General Who Guards the South and commander of Jing and Liang; Tao Kan took Jiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 使各帥所統以躡敦後。

translations.literal: each was ordered to lead his forces to follow Dun from behind.
translations.idiomatic: each was to march his forces in Dun's rear.

sentences.zh: 敦至石頭，欲攻劉隗。

translations.literal: Dun reached Stone City and wanted to attack Liu Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun reached Stone City intending to strike Liu Wei.

sentences.zh: 杜弘言于敦曰：“劉隗死士衆多，未易可克，不如攻石頭。

translations.literal: Du Hong said to Dun, "Liu Wei has many soldiers willing to die for him—not easy to overcome; better attack Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong told Dun, "Liu Wei has too many men who will fight to the death—Stone City is the softer target.

sentences.zh: 周札少恩，兵不爲用，攻之必敗，札敗則隗自走矣。

translations.literal: Zhou Zha has little kindness; his troops will not fight for him—attack and he will surely fail; once Zha fails, Wei will flee on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zha has never won his men's hearts—they will not stand for him. Take Stone City and he falls; then Liu Wei will run on his own.

sentences.zh: ”敦從之，以弘爲前鋒，攻石頭，札果開門納弘。

translations.literal: Dun followed this; made Hong vanguard; attacked Stone City; Zha indeed opened the gates and admitted Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Dun took his advice, made Du Hong vanguard, and attacked Stone City—and Zhou Zha opened the gates to let Hong in.

sentences.zh: 敦據石頭。

translations.literal: Dun occupied Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun seized Stone City.

sentences.zh: 嘆曰：“吾不復得爲盛德事矣！

translations.literal: He sighed, saying, "I can no longer serve the Emperor of Abundant Virtue!
translations.idiomatic: He sighed: "I can no longer serve a sovereign of perfect virtue!

sentences.zh: ”謝鯤曰：“何爲其然也！

translations.literal: Xie Kun said, "Why should that be so!
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun said, "Why say that?

sentences.zh: 但使自今已往，日忘日去耳。

translations.literal: Only let from this day forward each day forget the one before."
translations.idiomatic: From today on, let each day erase the one before."

sentences.zh: 帝命刁協、劉隗、戴淵帥衆攻石頭，王導、周顗、郭逸、虞潭等三道出戰，協等兵皆大敗。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Diao Xie, Liu Wei, and Dai Yuan to lead troops against Stone City; Wang Dao, Zhou Yi, Guo Yi, Yu Tan, and others advanced in three columns—all were heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Diao Xie, Liu Wei, and Dai Yuan against Stone City while Wang Dao, Zhou Yi, Guo Yi, and Yu Tan advanced in three columns—all were routed.

sentences.zh: 太子紹聞之，欲自帥將士决戰；

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Shao heard, he wished to lead officers and men himself to a decisive battle;
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Shao heard, he meant to lead the troops himself to a final battle;

sentences.zh: 升車將出，中庶子溫嶠執鞚諫曰：“殿下國之儲副，奈何以身輕天下！

translations.literal: mounting his carriage to go out, the junior mentor Wen Jiao seized the reins and remonstrated, saying, "Your Highness is the realm's heir—how can you lightly risk yourself for the empire!
translations.idiomatic: As he mounted his carriage to ride out, Wen Jiao, junior mentor to the heir, seized the reins: "Your Highness is the heir to the realm—how can you stake the empire on your own person!

sentences.zh: ”抽劍斬鞅，乃止。

translations.literal: He drew his sword and cut the crossbar, and [the prince] stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword and cut the crossbar—and the prince turned back.

sentences.zh: 敦擁兵不朝，放士卒劫掠，宮省奔散，惟安東將軍劉超按兵直衛，及侍中二人侍帝側。

translations.literal: Dun held his army without attending court, let soldiers plunder; palace offices scattered in flight—only Pacifier of the East Liu Chao held his troops on straight guard, and two attendants stood beside the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun kept his army from court and let his men loot; the palace emptied in panic—only Liu Chao, Pacifier of the East, held his ranks on guard, with two attendants at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 帝脫戎衣，著朝服，顧而言曰：“欲得我處，當早言！

translations.literal: The emperor removed military dress and put on court robes, turning to say, "If you want my place, speak early!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shed his armor for court dress and said, "If you want the throne, say so plainly!

sentences.zh: 何至害民如此！

translations.literal: Why go so far as to harm the people like this!
translations.idiomatic: Why visit such harm on the people!

sentences.zh: ”又遣使謂敦曰：“公若不忘本朝，于此息兵，則天下尚可共安。

translations.literal: He also sent a messenger to Dun, saying, "If you do not forget this dynasty, halt arms here, and the realm may still be shared in peace.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent word to Dun: "If you still honor this house, halt here and the realm may yet know peace together.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，朕當歸琅邪以避賢路。

translations.literal: If not, I shall return to Langye to yield the path to the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: If not, I shall withdraw to Langye and yield the throne to worthier men.

sentences.zh: 刁協、劉隗既敗，俱入宮，見帝于太極東除。

translations.literal: Diao Xie and Liu Wei having been defeated, both entered the palace and saw the emperor at the eastern steps of Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After their defeat Diao Xie and Liu Wei both entered the palace and found the emperor on the eastern steps of Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝執協、隗手，流涕嗚咽，勸令避禍。

translations.literal: The emperor took their hands, weeping and sobbing, urging them to flee for safety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took their hands, weeping, and urged them to flee and save themselves.

sentences.zh: 協曰：“臣當守死，不敢有貳。

translations.literal: Xie said, "I should die loyal—I dare not have a second loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Xie said, "I will die loyal—I cannot serve two masters.

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“今事逼矣，安可不行！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Matters press now—how can you not go!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Matters are desperate—you must go!

sentences.zh: ”乃令給協、隗人馬，使自爲計。

translations.literal: He then ordered men and horses given to Xie and Wei to plan their own escape.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them horses and men and told them to save themselves as they could.

sentences.zh: 協老，不堪騎乘，素無恩紀，募從者，皆委之，行至江乘，爲人所殺，送首于敦。

translations.literal: Xie was old, unable to ride; he had never shown kindness—those he recruited as followers all abandoned him; reaching Jiangcheng he was killed by someone who sent his head to Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was old and could not ride; he had never won loyalty—every follower he gathered deserted him. At Jiangcheng someone killed him and sent his head to Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 隗奔後趙，官至太子太傅而卒。

translations.literal: Wei fled to Later Zhao, rose to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei fled to Later Zhao, rose to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and died there.

sentences.zh: 帝令公卿百官詣石頭見敦，敦謂戴淵曰：“前日之戰，有餘力乎？

translations.literal: The emperor ordered civil and military officials to go to Stone City to see Dun; Dun said to Dai Yuan, "In battle the other day, did you have strength to spare?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the court to present themselves at Stone City. Wang Dun asked Dai Yuan, "In the fight the other day—did you still have strength to spare?

sentences.zh: ”淵曰：“豈敢有餘，但力不足耳！

translations.literal: Yuan said, "How dare I have spare strength—only that my strength was insufficient!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "Spare strength? I had none to spare—only too little!

sentences.zh: ”敦曰：“吾今此舉，天下以爲何如？

translations.literal: Dun said, "This campaign of mine—what does the realm call it?
translations.idiomatic: Dun said, "What does the realm call this campaign of mine?

sentences.zh: ”淵曰：“見形者謂之逆，體誠者謂之忠。

translations.literal: Yuan said, "Those who see the form call it rebellion; those who grasp the substance call it loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "Those who judge by appearances call it rebellion; those who know your heart call it loyalty.

sentences.zh: ”敦笑曰：“卿可謂能言。

translations.literal: Dun laughed, "You can truly speak.
translations.idiomatic: Dun laughed: "You have a nimble tongue.

sentences.zh: ”又謂周顗曰：“伯仁，卿負我！

translations.literal: He also said to Zhou Yi, "Boren, you have failed me!
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Zhou Yi: "Boren—you betrayed me!

sentences.zh: ”顗曰：“公戎車犯順，下官親帥六軍，不能其事，使王旅奔敗，以此負公。

translations.literal: Yi said, "Your lordship's war-chariot violated the throne; this humble official personally led the Six Armies and could not succeed—made the royal host flee in defeat; it is for that I have failed your lordship.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Your war-chariot marched against the throne; I led the Six Armies in person and failed—the royal host fled in rout. It is for that I have failed you.

sentences.zh: 辛未，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinwei, a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 以敦爲丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事、江州牧，封武昌郡公；

translations.literal: Dun was made Chancellor, commander of all internal and external forces, recorder of secretariat affairs, governor of Jiang Province, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wuchang Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun was named Chancellor, commander of all armies at home and abroad, recorder of the Secretariat, governor of Jiangzhou, and Duke of Wuchang;

sentences.zh: 幷讓不受。

translations.literal: he declined both and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: he declined them all and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 初，西都覆沒，四方皆勸進于帝。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the western capital fell, all quarters urged advancement upon the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the fall of the western capital, rulers everywhere urged him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 敦欲專國政，忌帝年長難制，欲更議所立，王導不從。

translations.literal: Dun wished to monopolize state affairs, feared the emperor's advanced age would make him hard to control, wished to deliberate anew on whom to install, Wang Dao would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Dun meant to seize the government; finding the emperor grown and hard to manage, he wanted to name another ruler—Wang Dao refused.

sentences.zh: 及敦克建康，謂導曰：“不用吾言，幾至覆族。

translations.literal: When Dun captured Jiankang, he said to Dao: "Had you not followed my words, [your clan] would nearly have been overthrown root and branch.
translations.idiomatic: After Dun took Jiankang, he told Dao, "Had you taken my advice, your entire house would have been wiped out.

sentences.zh: 敦以太子有勇略，爲朝野所向，欲誣以不孝而廢之。

translations.literal: Dun, because the heir apparent had courage and stratagem and was the object of court and countryside alike, wished to slander him with lack of filial piety and depose him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's courage and craft had won him the court and the realm; Dun plotted to charge him with unfilial conduct and remove him.

sentences.zh: 大會百官，問溫嶠曰：“皇太子以何德稱？

translations.literal: He gathered all officials in great assembly and asked Wen Jiao: "By what virtue does the heir apparent deserve his name?
translations.idiomatic: He convened the officials and asked Wen Jiao, "What merit does the heir apparent claim?

sentences.zh: ”聲色俱厲。

translations.literal: " His voice and bearing were both fierce.
translations.idiomatic: " His tone was savage, his manner threatening.

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：“鈎深致遠，蓋非淺局所量。

translations.literal: Jiao said: "Probing the deep and reaching the far—surely not what a shallow measure can gauge.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao said, "He plumbs depths and spans distances—a shallow eye cannot take his measure.

sentences.zh: 以禮觀之，可謂孝矣。

translations.literal: Viewed by ritual, he may be called filial.
translations.idiomatic: By the standards of propriety, one may call him filial.

sentences.zh: ”衆皆以爲信然，敦謀遂沮。

translations.literal: " All held it credible; Dun's plot then faltered.
translations.idiomatic: " The assembly believed him; Dun's design foundered.

sentences.zh: 帝召周顗于廣室，謂之曰：“近日大事，二宮無恙，諸人平安，大將軍固副所望邪？

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Zhou Yi to the broad chamber and said to him: "In these recent great affairs, are the Two Palaces unharmed, are all men at peace, has the Grand General indeed met what was hoped?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhou Yi to the great hall and asked, "In the crisis of late, are the Two Palaces safe, are the ministers unharmed—has the Grand General truly delivered what we hoped?

sentences.zh: ”顗曰：“二宮自如明詔，臣等尚未可知。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "The Two Palaces are as in Your Majesty's clear edicts; we ministers are not yet able to know.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi replied, "The palaces are as Your Majesty's edicts proclaim; as for us ministers, we cannot yet say.

sentences.zh: ”護軍長史郝嘏等勸顗避敦，顗曰：“吾備位大臣，朝廷喪敗，寧可複草間求活，外投胡、越邪！

translations.literal: " Protector-general chief clerk Hao Ga and others urged Yi to avoid Dun; Yi said: "I occupy a minister's post in name; the court is lost and ruined—how could I again seek life in the grass, cast myself outward to the Hu and Yue!
translations.idiomatic: " Hao Ga and others urged him to flee Dun. Yi said, "I hold rank among the great officers; the dynasty lies in ruin—shall I scrabble in the weeds for my life, or throw myself to barbarians beyond the pass?

sentences.zh: 敦參軍呂猗，嘗爲台郎，性奸諂，戴淵爲尚書，惡之。

translations.literal: Dun's aide-de-camp Lü Yi had once served as capital clerk, nature treacherous and fawning; Dai Yuan as Director of the Imperial Secretariat detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's staff officer Lü Yi had once been a capital clerk—a sycophant whom Dai Yuan, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, despised.

sentences.zh: 猗說敦曰：“周顗、戴淵，皆有高名，足以惑衆，近者之言，曾無怍色，公不除之，恐必有再舉之憂。

translations.literal: Yi said to Dun: "Zhou Yi and Dai Yuan both have lofty reputations sufficient to beguile the multitude; their recent words showed not the least flush of shame—if the lord does not eliminate them, I fear there must be the worry of their raising [troops] again.
translations.idiomatic: Yi told Dun, "Zhou Yi and Dai Yuan command such renown that they can sway the crowd; in their recent speeches they showed not a flicker of shame. Unless you remove them, they may rise against you again.

sentences.zh: ”敦素忌二人之才，心頗然之，從容問王導曰：“周、戴南北之望，當登三司無疑也。

translations.literal: " Dun had long envied the two men's talent, in his heart quite assented, and at leisure asked Wang Dao: "Zhou and Dai are the hopes of north and south—to ascend the Three Excellencies would be without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: " Dun had long resented their gifts; he agreed at once, and casually asked Wang Dao, "Zhou and Dai are luminaries of north and south—surely destined for the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: ”導不答。

translations.literal: " Dao did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Dao said nothing.

sentences.zh: 又曰：“若不三司，止應令僕邪？

translations.literal: Again he said: "If not the Three Excellencies, should they stop at Minister and Vice-Minister?
translations.idiomatic: Dun pressed, "If not that high, at least Minister and Vice-Minister?

sentences.zh: ”又不答。

translations.literal: " Again no answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Still silence.

sentences.zh: 敦曰：“若不爾，正當誅爾！

translations.literal: Dun said: "If not so, they ought rightly to be put to death!
translations.idiomatic: Dun said, "Otherwise they must die!

sentences.zh: ”又不答。

translations.literal: " Again no answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Still silence.

sentences.zh: 丙子，敦遣部將陳郡鄧岳收顗及淵。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Dun sent his commandery colonel Deng Yue of Chen to take Yi and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Dun sent Deng Yue of Chen commandery to seize Yi and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 先是，敦謂謝鯤曰：“吾當以周伯仁爲尚書令，戴若思爲僕射。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dun had told Xie Kun: "I shall make Zhou Bo-ren Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Dai Ruosi Vice-Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dun had told Xie Kun, "I mean to appoint Zhou Bo-ren Director of the Secretariat and Dai Ruosi Vice-Minister.

sentences.zh: ”是日，又問鯤：“近來人情何如？

translations.literal: " That day he again asked Kun: "How is popular feeling of late?
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he asked again, "What is the mood among the people?

sentences.zh: ”鯤曰：“明公之舉，雖欲大存社稷，然悠悠之言，實未達高義。

translations.literal: " Kun said: "The lord's action, though wishing greatly to preserve the altars of state, yet among loose talk truly has not reached lofty righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: " Kun said, "Though you mean to save the realm, common talk has not caught your larger purpose.

sentences.zh: 若果能舉用周、戴，則群情貼然矣！

translations.literal: If you can truly raise and employ Zhou and Dai, then the multitude's feelings will cling close.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly appoint Zhou and Dai, sentiment will settle at once.

sentences.zh: ”敦怒曰：“君粗疏邪！

translations.literal: " Dun angrily said: "Are you coarse and careless!
translations.idiomatic: " Dun snapped, "Are you that careless?

sentences.zh: 二子不相當，吾已收之矣！

translations.literal: The two men are not suited; I have already seized them!
translations.idiomatic: They are unfit—I have already taken them!

sentences.zh: ”鯤愕然自失。

translations.literal: " Kun stood stunned and bereft.
translations.idiomatic: " Kun stood stricken dumb.

sentences.zh: 參軍王嶠曰：“‘濟濟多士，文王以寧。

translations.literal: Aide Wang Jiao said: "'Abundant were the officers, and King Wen thereby had peace.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Wang Jiao said, "'With officers many and splendid, King Wen won his peace.

sentences.zh: ’奈何戮諸名士！

translations.literal: ' How can you slaughter such famed scholars!
translations.idiomatic: How can you kill men of such renown!

sentences.zh: ”敦大怒，欲斬嶠，衆莫敢言。

translations.literal: " Dun was greatly enraged and wished to behead Jiao; none in the crowd dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: " Dun flew into a rage and would have executed Jiao; none dared protest.

sentences.zh: 鯤曰：“明公舉大事，不戮一人。

translations.literal: Kun said: "When the lord undertakes great affairs, he does not put a single man to death.
translations.idiomatic: Kun said, "When the lord undertakes a great cause, he spares even one life.

sentences.zh: 嶠以獻替忤旨，便以釁鼓，不亦過乎！

translations.literal: Jiao, for remonstrance and substitution that offended the command, would be made war-offering at once—is this not excessive!
translations.idiomatic: Jiao only spoke against your will—must he die on the altar of war? That is too far!

sentences.zh: ”敦乃釋之，黜爲領軍長史。

translations.literal: " Dun thereupon released him, demoted to chief clerk of the Protector-general.
translations.idiomatic: " Dun released him and demoted him to chief clerk of the Protector-general's staff.

sentences.zh: 嶠，渾之族孫也。

translations.literal: Jiao was a clansman grandson of Wang Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was a descendant of Wang Hun's clan.

sentences.zh: 顗被收，路經太廟，大言曰：“賊臣王敦，傾覆社稷，枉殺忠臣。

translations.literal: Yi being taken, the road passed the Grand Ancestral Temple; he spoke loudly: "The traitor minister Wang Dun overturns the altars of state and wrongly kills loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: As Yi was led away, his route passed the imperial temple; he cried out, "The rebel Wang Dun overthrows the state and murders loyal servants without cause.

sentences.zh: 神祇有靈，當速殺之！

translations.literal: If the spirits and gods have numinous power, let them swiftly kill him!
translations.idiomatic: O gods, if you have power, strike him down at once!

sentences.zh: ”收人以戟傷其口，血流至踵，容止自若，觀者皆爲流涕。

translations.literal: " Those who took him used halberds to wound his mouth; blood flowed to his heels, deportment calm as ever; all who watched wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: " His captors gashed his mouth with halberds; blood ran to his heels, yet he bore himself as calmly as before, and onlookers wept.

sentences.zh: 幷戴淵殺之于石頭南門之外。

translations.literal: Together with Dai Yuan they were killed outside the Southern Gate of Stone Town.
translations.idiomatic: He and Dai Yuan were put to death outside the southern gate of Stone Fort.

sentences.zh: 帝使侍中王彬勞敦。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Attendant-in-ordinary Wang Bin to console Dun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wang Bin, Palace Attendant, to congratulate Dun.

sentences.zh: 彬素與顗善，先往哭顗，然後見敦。

translations.literal: Bin had long been on good terms with Yi; he first went to weep for Yi, then came to see Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had been Zhou Yi's friend; he mourned Yi first, then presented himself to Dun.

sentences.zh: 敦怪其容慘，問之。

translations.literal: Dun wondered at his mournful bearing and asked.
translations.idiomatic: Dun noted his grief-stricken face and asked the reason.

sentences.zh: 彬曰：“向哭伯仁，情不能已。

translations.literal: Bin said: "Just now weeping for Bo-ren—feeling could not be stayed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "I have been weeping for Bo-ren; I could not help myself.

sentences.zh: ”敦怒曰：“伯仁自致刑戮；

translations.literal: " Dun angrily said: "Bo-ren brought execution on himself;
translations.idiomatic: " Dun snapped, "Bo-ren brought death on himself;

sentences.zh: 且凡人遇汝，汝何哀而哭之？

translations.literal: moreover, when an ordinary man meets you, why do you mourn and weep for him?
translations.idiomatic: besides, he was nobody to you—why weep?

sentences.zh: ”彬曰：“伯仁長者，兄之親友；

translations.literal: " Bin said: "Bo-ren was an elder of worth, your elder brother's friend;
translations.idiomatic: " Bin said, "Bo-ren was a man of stature, your brother's intimate;

sentences.zh: 在朝雖無謇愕，亦非阿黨，赦後加之極刑，所以傷惋也。

translations.literal: in court though without blunt remonstrance, yet was not partisan clique; after amnesty yet subjected to extreme punishment—hence my wounded grief.
translations.idiomatic: in court he neither thundered against you nor joined your faction; after the general amnesty you condemned him to death—that is what wounds me.

sentences.zh: ”因勃然數敦曰：“兄抗旌犯順，殺戮忠良，圖爲不軌，禍及門戶矣！

translations.literal: " Thereupon he fiercely counted Dun's crimes: "Elder brother raises banners against right, slaughters the loyal and good, plots irregular acts—calamity will reach the household!
translations.idiomatic: " Then he rounded on Dun: "Brother, you have raised arms against your sovereign, slaughtered the loyal, and set your heart on treason—ruin will come to our house!

sentences.zh: ”辭氣慷慨，聲泪俱下。

translations.literal: " His words and breath were ardent; voice and tears fell together.
translations.idiomatic: " His words rang with fury; tears streamed with his voice.

sentences.zh: 敦大怒，厲聲曰：“爾狂悖乃至此，以吾爲不能殺汝邪！

translations.literal: Dun was greatly enraged, voice severe: "You are so wildly perverse as this—you think I cannot kill you!
translations.idiomatic: Dun thundered, "You are mad enough to think I cannot kill you!

sentences.zh: ”時王導在坐，爲之懼，勸彬起謝。

translations.literal: " At that time Wang Dao was seated present, feared for him, urged Bin to rise and apologize.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dao, who was present, trembled for him and urged Bin to rise and apologize.

sentences.zh: 彬曰：“脚痛不能拜！

translations.literal: Bin said: "My foot pains—I cannot bow!
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "My feet hurt—I cannot kneel!

sentences.zh: 且此複何謝！

translations.literal: Moreover, for this why apologize again!
translations.idiomatic: And what would I apologize for?

sentences.zh: ”敦曰：“脚痛孰若頸痛！

translations.literal: " Dun said: "Foot pain—how does it compare with neck pain!
translations.idiomatic: " Dun said, "A sore foot is nothing beside a sore neck!

sentences.zh: ”彬殊無懼容，竟不肯拜。

translations.literal: " Bin wholly without fear on his countenance, to the end would not bow.
translations.idiomatic: " Bin never flinched and would not bow.

sentences.zh: 王導後料檢中書故事，乃見顗救己之表，執之流涕曰：“吾雖不殺伯仁，伯仁由我而死，幽冥之中，負此良友！

translations.literal: Later Wang Dao examined Secretariat precedents and saw Yi's memorial saving him; clutching it he wept and said: "Though I did not kill Bo-ren, Bo-ren died through me—in the dark void I have failed this fine friend!
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Dao searched the Secretariat archives and found Yi's memorial pleading for his life; clutching it he wept and said, "I did not strike the blow, yet Bo-ren died for me—in the shades I owe this friend a debt I can never repay!

sentences.zh: ”沈充拔吳國，殺內史張茂。

translations.literal: " Shen Chong took Wu commandery and killed Grand administrator Zhang Mao.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Chong overran Wu commandery and slew its grand administrator, Zhang Mao.

sentences.zh: 初，王敦聞甘卓起兵，大懼。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Dun hearing Gan Zhuo raised troops, was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun first learned that Gan Zhuo had taken the field, he was terrified.

sentences.zh: 卓兄子卬爲敦參軍，敦使卬歸卓曰：“君此自是臣節，不相責也。

translations.literal: Zhuo's elder brother's son Ang was Dun's aide-de-camp; Dun sent Ang back to Zhuo saying: "Your lord's action here is itself a minister's duty; I do not blame you.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's nephew Ang served on Dun's staff; Dun sent him back with a message: "Your move is the duty of a loyal officer; I do not hold it against you.

sentences.zh: 吾家計急，不得不爾。

translations.literal: Our family's plans are urgent; I could not but do this.
translations.idiomatic: My house is in desperate straits; I had no choice.

sentences.zh: 想便旋軍襄陽，當更結好。

translations.literal: I think you will soon wheel the army to Xiangyang; we shall renew our bond.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw to Xiangyang and we shall make peace again.

sentences.zh: ”卓雖慕忠義，性多疑少决，軍于猪口，欲待諸方同出軍，稽留累旬不前。

translations.literal: " Zhuo, though admiring loyalty and righteousness, by nature was much doubting and short on resolve; the army at Zhukou, wishing to wait for all quarters to issue troops together, delayed and lingered many weeks without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuo admired loyalty but was indecisive and suspicious; his army halted at Zhukou, waiting for allies to march together, and for many weeks he did not advance.

sentences.zh: 敦既得建康。

translations.literal: Dun having already taken Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: After Dun had secured Jiankang,

sentences.zh: 乃遣台使以騶虞幡駐卓軍。

translations.literal: thereupon sent the court's messenger with the zouyu banner to halt Zhuo's army.
translations.idiomatic: he sent an imperial envoy bearing the zouyu banner to bring Zhuo's army to a halt.

sentences.zh: 卓聞周顗、戴淵死，流涕謂卬曰：“吾之所憂，正爲今日。

translations.literal: Zhuo hearing Zhou Yi and Dai Yuan dead, shedding tears said to Ang: "What I feared is precisely for this day.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Zhou Yi and Dai Yuan's deaths, Zhuo wept and told Ang, "This is the day I dreaded.

sentences.zh: 且使聖上元吉，太子無恙，吾臨敦上流，亦未敢遽危社稷。

translations.literal: Moreover, were the sage sovereign wholly fortunate, the heir unharmed, I pressing Dun upstream yet would not dare hastily endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: If the Son of Heaven were safe and the crown prince unharmed, I could hold the river above Dun and still refrain from endangering the realm.

sentences.zh: 適吾徑據武昌，敦勢逼，必劫天子以絕四海之望，不如還襄陽，更思後圖。

translations.literal: Just now I have straight taken Wuchang; Dun's power presses—he will surely seize the Son of Heaven to cut off all the realm's hopes; better to return to Xiangyang and reconsider a later plan.
translations.idiomatic: But I have seized Wuchang; Dun's strength presses close—he will seize the emperor and dash every hope in the empire. Better withdraw to Xiangyang and plot anew.

sentences.zh: ”即命旋軍。

translations.literal: " He at once ordered the army to wheel back.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the army to withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 都尉秦康與樂道融說卓曰：“今分兵斷彭澤，使敦上下不得相赴，其衆自然離散，可一戰擒也。

translations.literal: Commandant Qin Kang and Yue Daorong said to Zhuo: "Now divide troops to cut Pengze, so Dun above and below cannot meet each other; his host will naturally scatter—you can capture him in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Kang and Yue Daorong urged Zhuo, "Split your force and block Pengze, so Dun's armies cannot join; his men will melt away, and you can take him in one fight.

sentences.zh: 將軍起義兵而中止，竊爲將軍不取。

translations.literal: The general raised righteous troops yet halts—I privately deem it unworthy of the general.
translations.idiomatic: You raised a righteous army only to halt—I fear that is a mistake.

sentences.zh: 且將軍之下，士卒各求其利，欲求西還，亦恐不可得也。

translations.literal: Moreover, under the general, officers and soldiers each seek their own profit; wishing to return west, I fear it may likewise not be obtainable.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your soldiers fight for their own gain; even if you wished to march west again, they might not follow.

sentences.zh: ”卓不從。

translations.literal: " Zhuo would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuo would not listen.

sentences.zh: 道融晝夜泣諫，卓不聽；

translations.literal: Daorong by day and night wept in remonstrance; Zhuo would not heed;
translations.idiomatic: Daorong pleaded day and night with tears; Zhuo ignored him;

sentences.zh: 道融憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: Daorong died of worried indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Daorong died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 卓性本寬和，忽更强塞，徑還襄陽，意氣騷擾，舉動失常，識者知其將死矣。

translations.literal: Zhuo's nature was originally mild and harmonious; suddenly he became more forceful and obstructive, marched straight back to Xiangyang, spirit and breath agitated, conduct and movement abnormal—those who understood knew he would soon die.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo had always been mild; now he turned harsh, marching straight for Xiangyang, restless and erratic in all he did—men of judgment knew he was doomed.

sentences.zh: 王敦以西陽王羕爲太宰，加王導尚書令，王廙爲荊州刺史；

translations.literal: Wang Dun made the Prince of Xiyang, Yang, Grand Mentor, added Wang Dao as Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Wang Yi as Inspector of Jing province;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun appointed Prince Xi of Xiyang Grand Mentor, made Wang Dao Director of the Secretariat, and Wang Yi inspector of Jing province;

sentences.zh: 改易百官及諸軍鎮，轉徙黜免者以百數；

translations.literal: changed and replaced the hundred officials and all military garrisons; transferred, shifted, dismissed and removed—those counted in the hundreds;
translations.idiomatic: he shuffled hundreds of officials and garrison commanders, transferring or dismissing them wholesale;

sentences.zh: 或朝行暮改，惟意所欲。

translations.literal: some enacted in the morning, changed at evening—only as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: some officeholders gained a post at dawn and lost it by dusk, all at his whim.

sentences.zh: 敦將還武昌，謝鯤言于敦曰：“公至都以來，稱疾不朝，是以雖建勛而人心實有未達。

translations.literal: Dun about to return to Wuchang; Xie Kun spoke to Dun: "Since the lord reached the capital you have pleaded illness and not attended court—thus though you have built merit, in people's hearts truly there is what has not been understood.
translations.idiomatic: As Dun prepared to return to Wuchang, Xie Kun said, "Since you reached the capital you have stayed away from court on pretext of illness; though your merit is real, men still do not understand your purpose.

sentences.zh: 今若朝天子，使君臣釋然，則物情皆悅服矣。

translations.literal: Now if you attend court before the Son of Heaven and let lord and minister release their cares, then the world's feelings will all be pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: If you now attend the emperor and put court and throne at ease, the realm will gladly follow you.

sentences.zh: ”敦曰：“君能保無變乎？

translations.literal: " Dun said: "Can you guarantee there will be no change?
translations.idiomatic: " Dun said, "Can you guarantee nothing will go wrong?

sentences.zh: ”對曰：“鯤近日入覲，主上側席，遲得見公，宮省穆然，必無虞也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Kun of late entered audience; the lord-on-high sat sidelong on his mat, delayed in meeting the lord; palace and offices were solemnly still—surely without worry.
translations.idiomatic: " Kun said, "I have just been received in audience; the emperor waits on edge for you; the palace is calm—there is no danger.

sentences.zh: 公若入朝，鯤請侍從。

translations.literal: If the lord enters court, Kun asks to attend and follow.
translations.idiomatic: If you will go to court, I beg leave to attend you.

sentences.zh: ”敦勃然曰：“正複殺君等數百人，亦複何損于時！
