translations.literal: " Dun erupted: "Even if I again kill you and several hundred others—what further loss to the age!
translations.idiomatic: " Dun exploded, "I could kill you and a few hundred more—what difference would it make?

sentences.zh: ”竟不朝而去。

translations.literal: " To the end he did not attend court but left.
translations.idiomatic: " He never went to court and departed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，敦還武昌。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Dun returned to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Dun withdrew to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 初，宜都內史天門周級聞譙王承起兵，使其兄子該潜詣長沙，申款于承。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou Ji of Tianmen, Grand Administrator of Yidu, hearing Prince of Qiao Wang Cheng raised troops, sent his elder brother's son Gai in secret to Changsha to declare earnest loyalty to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhou Ji of Tianmen, grand administrator of Yidu, learned that Prince Qiao Wang Cheng had taken up arms; he sent his nephew Gai in secret to Changsha to pledge fealty.

sentences.zh: 魏乂等攻湘州急，承遣該及從事邵陵周崎間出求救，皆爲邏者所得。

translations.literal: Wei Yi and others pressed the attack on Xiang province urgently; Cheng sent Gai and his aide Zhou Qi of Shaoling by detour to seek rescue, all were taken by scouts on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yi and others pressed Hunan hard; Cheng sent Gai and his staff officer Zhou Qi of Shaoling to break through for aid, but scouts seized them both.

sentences.zh: 又使崎語城中，稱大將軍已克建康，甘卓還襄陽，外援理絕。

translations.literal: Again he sent Qi to speak to the city, declaring the Grand General had already taken Jiankang, Gan Zhuo returned to Xiangyang, outside aid logically cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qi to tell the city that the Grand General had taken Jiankang, Gan Zhuo had withdrawn to Xiangyang, and all hope of relief was gone.

sentences.zh: 崎僞許之，既至城下，大呼曰：“援兵尋至，努力堅守！

translations.literal: Qi falsely assented; having reached below the wall, he shouted loudly: "Rescue troops will soon arrive—strive to hold firm!
translations.idiomatic: Qi pretended to agree; at the foot of the wall he shouted, "Relief is near—hold on with all your strength!

sentences.zh: ”乂殺之。

translations.literal: " Yi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi executed him.

sentences.zh: 乂考該至死，竟不言其故，周級由是獲免。

translations.literal: Yi examined Gai to death; to the end he did not speak its reason—Zhou Ji thereby obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Yi tortured Gai to death, but Gai never revealed the plot, and Zhou Ji was spared.

sentences.zh: 乂等攻戰日逼，敦又送所得台中人書疏，令乂射以示承。

translations.literal: Yi and others pressed the attack day by day; Dun again sent captured court men's letters and memorials, ordered Yi to shoot them in to show Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The siege tightened daily; Dun forwarded captured court documents and had Yi shoot them into the city to show Cheng.

sentences.zh: 城中知朝廷不守，莫不悵惋。

translations.literal: The city, knowing the court could not hold, none but were despondent and regretful.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the capital had fallen, the defenders were heartsick.

sentences.zh: 相持且百日，劉翼戰死，士卒死傷相枕。

translations.literal: They held each other off nearly a hundred days; Liu Yi died in battle, officers and soldiers dead and wounded piled pillow upon pillow.
translations.idiomatic: The standoff lasted nearly a hundred days; Liu Yi fell in battle, and the dead and wounded lay heaped upon one another.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，乂拔長沙，承等皆被執。

translations.literal: On guisi, Yi took Changsha; Cheng and all were taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Yi stormed Changsha and seized Cheng and his company.

sentences.zh: 乂將殺虞悝，子弟對之號泣。

translations.literal: Yi about to kill Yu Kui; sons and younger brothers facing him wailed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: As Yi prepared to execute Yu Kui, Kui's sons and nephews wept before him.

sentences.zh: 悝曰：“人生會當有死，今闔門爲忠義之鬼，亦複何恨！

translations.literal: Kui said: "Human life surely must have death; now the whole household becomes ghosts of loyalty and righteousness—what further regret!
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "Every life must end; if our whole house dies as ghosts of loyalty, what is there to regret?

sentences.zh: 乂以檻車載承及易雄送武昌，佐吏皆奔散，惟主簿桓雄、西曹書佐韓階、從事武延，毀服爲僮，從承，不離左右。

translations.literal: Yi used a prisoner cart to carry Cheng and Yi Xiong to Wuchang; the aides all fled and scattered, only Registrar Huan Xiong, Western Bureau Clerk Han Jie, and Staff Officer Wu Yan ruined their robes to pose as servants, followed Cheng, never leaving his side.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent Cheng and Yi Xiong to Wuchang in a caged cart; his staff scattered, but Registrar Huan Xiong, clerk Han Jie, and aide Wu Yan tore their clothes, disguised themselves as servants, and never left Cheng's side.

sentences.zh: 乂見桓雄姿貌舉止非凡人，憚而殺之。

translations.literal: Yi saw Huan Xiong's appearance and bearing were not those of an ordinary man, feared him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi saw that Huan Xiong's looks and manner were no common man's; afraid of him, he had him killed.

sentences.zh: 韓階、武延執志愈固。

translations.literal: Han Jie and Wu Yan held their resolve ever firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jie and Wu Yan only clung more stubbornly to their purpose.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史王廙承敦旨，殺承于道中，階、延送承喪至都，葬之而去。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Wang Yi carried out Dun's order, killed Cheng on the road; Jie and Yan escorted Cheng's coffin to the capital, buried him and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing inspector Wang Yi, acting on Dun's orders, killed Cheng on the road; Jie and Yan bore his coffin to the capital, buried him, and went their way.

sentences.zh: 易雄至武昌，意氣忼慨，曾無懼容。

translations.literal: Yi Xiong reached Wuchang, spirit bold and open, never a fearful look.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi Xiong reached Wuchang, his bearing was fierce and open; he never showed fear.

sentences.zh: 敦遣人以檄示雄而數之，雄曰：“此實有之，惜雄位微力弱，不能救國難耳。

translations.literal: Dun sent a man to show Xiong the proclamation and rebuke him; Xiong said: "This truly was so—alas Xiong's position was slight and strength weak, unable to save the state's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Dun sent someone to read him the indictment; Xiong said, "It is true—I was too small a man, too weak, to save the realm from disaster.

sentences.zh: 今日之死，固所願也！

translations.literal: Death today is what I have long wished for!
translations.idiomatic: To die today is what I have long wished for!

sentences.zh: ”敦憚其辭正，釋之，遣就舍。

translations.literal: " Dun feared his words were upright, released him, sent him to his lodging.
translations.idiomatic: " Dun, daunted by his plain courage, released him and sent him to his quarters.

sentences.zh: 衆人皆賀之，雄笑曰：“吾安得生！

translations.literal: All congratulated him; Xiong laughed: "How could I live!
translations.idiomatic: Everyone congratulated him; Xiong laughed and said, "How could I live?

sentences.zh: ”既而敦遣人潜殺之。

translations.literal: " Before long Dun sent men to secretly kill him.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon after, Dun had him murdered in secret.

sentences.zh: 魏乂求鄧騫甚急，鄉人皆爲之懼，騫笑曰：“此欲用我耳，彼新得州，多殺忠良，故求我以厭人望也。

translations.literal: Wei Yi urgently sought Deng Qian; villagers all feared for him, Qian laughed: "They wish to use me—the other newly got the province, killed many loyal and good, so they seek me to satisfy men's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yi was hunting Deng Qian hard; the villagers were afraid for him, but Qian laughed and said, "They want to use me. He has just taken the province and slaughtered many loyal men—they need me to satisfy the people's hopes.

sentences.zh: ”乃往詣乂。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went to visit Yi.
translations.idiomatic: " He went straight to Yi.

sentences.zh: 乂喜曰：“君，古之解揚也。

translations.literal: Yi delighted: "You are a Jieyang of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was delighted. "You are a Jieyang of old,

sentences.zh: ”以爲別駕。

translations.literal: " and made him Deputy Governor.
translations.idiomatic: " he said, and appointed him deputy governor.

sentences.zh: 詔以陶侃領湘州刺史；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Tao Kan to hold Inspector of Xiang province;
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Tao Kan acting inspector of Xiang province;

sentences.zh: 王敦上侃複還廣州，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Wang Dun memorialized the throne to return Kan again to Guangzhou, adding Gentleman Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun memorialized to send Kan back to Guangzhou and added the title Gentleman Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 甲午，前趙羊後卒，謚曰獻文。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Former Zhao's Yang Hou died, posthumous title Xianwen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Yang Hou of Former Zhao died; her posthumous title was Xianwen.

sentences.zh: 甘卓家人皆勸卓備王敦，卓不從，悉散兵佃作，聞諫，輒怒。

translations.literal: Gan Zhuo's household all urged Zhuo to prepare against Wang Dun, Zhuo would not follow, dismissed all troops to farming; hearing remonstrance, he always grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo's family urged him to guard against Wang Dun; he refused, sent all his soldiers back to the fields, and flew into a rage whenever anyone remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 襄陽太守周慮密承敦意，詐言湖中多魚，勸卓遣左右悉出捕魚。

translations.literal: Administrator of Xiangyang Zhou Lü secretly carried Dun's intent, falsely said many fish in the lake, urged Zhuo to send his attendants all out to catch fish.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang grand administrator Zhou Lü, secretly acting for Dun, claimed the lake was full of fish and persuaded Zhuo to send all his attendants out to net them.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙亥，慮引兵襲卓于寢室，殺之，傳首于敦，幷殺其諸子。

translations.literal: Fifth month, yihai, Lü led troops to surprise Zhuo in his bedchamber, killed him, sent the head to Dun, and killed all his sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yihai, Lü led troops into Zhuo's bedchamber, killed him, sent his head to Dun, and slew all his sons as well.

sentences.zh: 敦以從事中郎周撫督沔北諸軍事，代卓鎮沔中。

translations.literal: Dun made his aide Zhou Fu supervise all military affairs north of the Mian, replacing Zhuo to garrison the middle Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Dun made his aide Zhou Fu commander of all forces north of the Mian and sent him to replace Zhuo in the middle reaches.

sentences.zh: 撫，訪之子也。

translations.literal: Fu was the son of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was Zhou Fang's son.

sentences.zh: 敦既得志，暴慢滋甚，四方貢獻多入其府，將相岳牧皆出其門。

translations.literal: Dun having attained his will, violence and arrogance grew daily; tributes from all quarters mostly entered his mansion; ministers, generals, and governors all came from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dun had his way, his arrogance and violence only grew; tribute from every quarter flowed into his mansion, and ministers and governors alike owed their posts to him.

sentences.zh: 以沈充、錢鳳爲謀主，唯二人之言是從，所譖無不死者。

translations.literal: He took Shen Chong and Qian Feng as planners; only these two men's words he followed; those they slandered did not escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong and Qian Feng were his chief advisers; he followed only them, and no one they denounced escaped death.

sentences.zh: 以諸葛瑤、鄧岳、周撫、李恒、謝雍爲爪牙。

translations.literal: He took Zhuge Yao, Deng Yue, Zhou Fu, Li Heng, Xie Yong as claws and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Yao, Deng Yue, Zhou Fu, Li Heng, and Xie Yong served as his claws and fangs.

sentences.zh: 充等幷凶險驕恣，大起營府，侵人田宅，剽掠市道，識者鹹知其將敗焉。

translations.literal: Chong and the rest were alike fierce, dangerous, arrogant and wilful; they built camps and offices on a grand scale, encroached on men's fields and houses, plundered markets and roads—those who knew all said they would soon be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and his fellows were brutal, arrogant, and reckless; they threw up vast camps, seized fields and houses, and plundered the markets—everyone who could see ahead knew they were riding for a fall.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，後趙中山公虎拔泰山，執徐龕送襄國；

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Later Zhao's Duke of Zhongshan Hu took Mount Tai, seized Xu Kan and sent him to Xiangguo;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Shi Hu, Duke of Zhongshan of Later Zhao, took Mount Tai, seized Xu Kan, and sent him to Xiangguo;

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒盛之以囊，于百尺樓上撲殺之，命王伏都等妻子刳而食之，坑其降卒三千人。

translations.literal: Later Zhao King Le had him placed in a sack, at a hundred-foot tower flung him to death, ordered Wang Fudu's and others' wives and children disemboweled and eaten, buried three thousand surrendered soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's king Shi Le had Kan sewn into a sack and hurled from a hundred-foot tower to his death; he ordered Wang Fudu's family disemboweled and eaten, and buried alive three thousand surrendered troops.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史郗鑒在鄒山三年，有衆數萬。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yanzhou Xi Jian was at Mount Zou three years, with troops numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou inspector Xi Jian held Mount Zou for three years with an army of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 戰爭不息，百姓饑饉，掘野鼠、蟄燕而食之，爲後趙所逼，退屯合肥。

translations.literal: War unceasing, the people starved; they dug wild rats and hibernating swallows to eat; pressed by Later Zhao, he withdrew to garrison Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: War never ceased; the people starved and dug out wild rats and hibernating swallows to eat. Pressed by Later Zhao, he withdrew to Hefei.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射紀瞻，以鑒雅望清德，宜從容台閣，上疏請征之；

translations.literal: Minister of the Right Ji Zhan, because Jian's elegant reputation and pure virtue suited the ease of the central terrace, memorialized to summon him;
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan, Vice Minister of the Secretariat, argued that Jian's standing and integrity suited the central court and memorialized for his recall;

sentences.zh: 乃征拜尚書。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was summoned and appointed Minister.
translations.idiomatic: and Jian was summoned and appointed Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 徐、兗間諸塢多降于後趙，後趙置守宰以撫之。

translations.literal: Many walled strongholds between Xu and Yan mostly surrendered to Later Zhao; Later Zhao set guards and magistrates to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the fortified camps between Xu and Yan surrendered to Later Zhao, which installed officials to govern them.

sentences.zh: 王敦自領寧、益二州都督。

translations.literal: Wang Dun personally held the post of Area Commander of Ning and Yi provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun took for himself the area command of Ning and Yi provinces.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己丑，荊州刺史武陵康侯王廙卒。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, jichou, Inspector of Jing Wuling Kanghou Wang Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jichou, Jing inspector Wang Yi, Marquis Kang of Wuling, died.

sentences.zh: 王敦以下邳內史王邃都督青、徐、幽、平四州諸軍事，鎮淮陰；

translations.literal: Wang Dun made Grand Administrator of Xiapi Wang Sui Area Commander of Qing, Xu, You, and Ping, garrisoned Huaiyin;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun made Xiapi grand administrator Wang Sui area commander of Qing, Xu, You, and Ping and stationed him at Huaiyin;

sentences.zh: 衛將軍王含都督沔南諸軍事，領荊州刺史；

translations.literal: Defender-general Wang Han Area Commander of all military affairs south of the Mian, held Inspector of Jing;
translations.idiomatic: Defender-general Wang Han commanded all forces south of the Mian and held the post of Jing inspector;

sentences.zh: 武昌太守丹楊王諒爲交州刺史。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Wuchang Danyang Wang Liang was Inspector of Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang grand administrator Wang Liang of Danyang became inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 使諒收交州刺史修湛、新昌太守梁碩殺之。

translations.literal: Sent Liang to seize Inspector of Jiao Xiu Zhan and Grand Administrator of Xinchang Liang Shuo and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liang to seize Jiao inspector Xiu Zhan and Xinchang grand administrator Liang Shuo and kill them.

sentences.zh: 諒誘湛。

translations.literal: Liang lured Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang lured Zhan into a trap.

sentences.zh: 斬之。

translations.literal: Beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 碩舉兵圍諒于龍編。

translations.literal: Shuo raised troops and besieged Liang at Longbian.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo raised troops and besieged Liang at Longbian.

sentences.zh: 祖逖既卒，後越屢寇河南，拔襄城、城父，圍譙。

translations.literal: After Zu Ti died, the Yue repeatedly raided Henan, took Xiangcheng and Chengfù, besieged Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: After Zu Ti's death, the Later Yue repeatedly raided Henan, took Xiangcheng and Chengfù, and besieged Qiao.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史祖約不能禦，退屯壽春。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yu Zu Yue could not resist, withdrew to garrison Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu inspector Zu Yue could not hold them off and withdrew to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 後趙遂取陳留，梁、鄭之間複騷然矣。

translations.literal: Later Zhao then took Chenliu; between Liang and Zheng was turmoil again.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao then took Chenliu, and the lands between Liang and Zheng were in turmoil again.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以臨穎元公荀組爲太尉；

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Lin-ying Duke of Yuan Xun Zu was made Grand Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Xun Zu, Duke of Yuan of Linying, was made Grand Commandant;

sentences.zh: 辛酉，薨。

translations.literal: On xinyou, died.
translations.idiomatic: on xinyou he died.

sentences.zh: 罷司徒，幷丞相府。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education was abolished, merged with the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Education was abolished and merged with the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 王敦以司徒官屬爲留府。

translations.literal: Wang Dun made the Ministry of Education's staff as retainers in the leftover office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun kept the Ministry of Education's staff as retainers in the residual office.

sentences.zh: 帝憂憤成疾，閏月，己丑，崩。

translations.literal: The emperor worry and indignation became illness; intercalary month, jichou, died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sickened with grief and rage; in the intercalary month, on jichou, he died.

sentences.zh: 司空王導受遣詔輔政。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wang Dao received the edict to assist the government.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wang Dao received the late emperor's edict to assist the government.

sentences.zh: 帝恭儉有餘而明斷不足，故大業未複而禍亂內興。

translations.literal: The emperor was reverent and frugal in surplus but short on clear judgment; thus the great enterprise was not restored while calamity and disorder rose within.
translations.idiomatic: He had been reverent and frugal, but lacked decisive judgment; the great restoration never came, and calamity rose within the realm.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，太子即皇帝位，大赦，尊所生母荀氏爲建安君。

translations.literal: On gengyin the heir apparent ascended the emperor's throne, great amnesty, honored his birth-mother Lady Xun as Lady of Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the crown prince took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and honored his mother, Lady Xun, as Lady of Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 十二月，趙主曜葬其父母于粟邑，大赦。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Zhao ruler Liu Yao buried his parents at Suyi, great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Zhao ruler Liu Yao buried his parents at Suyi and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 陵下周二裏，上高百尺，計用六萬夫，作之百日乃成。

translations.literal: Around the mound two li, mound top a hundred feet high, reckoned sixty thousand laborers, completed in a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: The precinct around the mound measured two li; the mound rose a hundred feet; sixty thousand laborers were reckoned, and the work took a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 役者夜作，繼以脂燭，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Laborers worked by night, continued with grease lamps; the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: They labored by night under lamps of tallow; the people suffered bitterly.

sentences.zh: 游子遠諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Youzi Yuan remonstrated; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Youzi Yuan remonstrated, but Yao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 後趙濮陽景侯張賓卒，後趙王勒哭之慟，曰：“天不欲成吾事邪？

translations.literal: Later Zhao Puyang Marquis Zhang Bin died; Later Zhao King Le wept for him bitterly, said: "Does Heaven not wish to complete my affair?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin, Marquis Jing of Puyang of Later Zhao, died; King Shi Le wept bitterly and said, "Does Heaven not wish me to succeed?

sentences.zh: 何奪吾右侯之早也！

translations.literal: Why take our Right Lord so early!
translations.idiomatic: Why take my Right Lord so soon!

sentences.zh: ”程遐代爲右長史。

translations.literal: " Cheng Xia replaced as Right Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng Xia replaced him as Right Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 遐，世子弘之舅也，勒每與遐議，有所不合，輒嘆曰：“右侯舍我去，乃令我與此輩共事，豈非酷乎！

translations.literal: Xia was the heir Prince Hong's maternal uncle; whenever Le discussed with Xia and something did not agree, he would sigh: "The Right Lord left me—now I must share affairs with this crowd—is it not cruel!
translations.idiomatic: Xia was the crown prince Hong's uncle by marriage; whenever Le discussed matters with him and they disagreed, he would sigh, "The Right Lord has left me to share power with men like these—is that not cruel?

sentences.zh: ”因流涕彌日。

translations.literal: " And wept all day.
translations.idiomatic: " And wept all day.

sentences.zh: 張茂使將軍韓璞帥衆取隴西、南安之地，置秦州。

translations.literal: Zhang Mao sent General Han Pu leading troops to take Longxi and Nan'an territory, set up Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao sent General Han Pu to seize Longxi and Nan'an and established Qin province.

sentences.zh: 慕容廆遣其世子皝襲段末柸，入令支，掠其居民千餘家而還。

translations.literal: Murong Hui sent his heir Murong Huang to attack Duan Moqi, entered Lingzhi, plundered more than a thousand households of its people and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui sent his heir Murong Huang against Duan Moqi; Huang entered Lingzhi, carried off more than a thousand households, and returned.

sentences.zh: 中宗元皇帝下太寧元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong Yuan, Part Two, Taining Year One (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of the Middle House, Part Two — Year One of Taining (

sentences.zh: 癸未，公元三二三年）

translations.literal: guiwei, year CE 323)
translations.idiomatic: guiwei, CE 323)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，成李驤、任回寇台登，將軍司馬玖戰死，越巂太守李釗、漢嘉太守王載皆以郡降于成。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Cheng's Li Xiang and Ren Hui raided Taideng; General Sima Jiu died in battle; Grand Administrator of Yuexi Li Zhao and Grand Administrator of Hanjia Wang Zai both surrendered their commanderies to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Li Xiang and Ren Hui of Cheng raided Taideng; General Sima Jiu fell in battle; Yuexi grand administrator Li Zhao and Hanjia grand administrator Wang Zai surrendered their commanderies to Cheng.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚戌，葬元帝于建平陵。

translations.literal: Second month, gengxu, buried the Yuan Emperor at Jianping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengxu, the Yuan Emperor was buried at Jianping Tomb.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊寅朔，改元。

translations.literal: Third month, first day wuyin, changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month, wuyin, the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 饒安、東光、安陵三縣灾，燒七千餘家，死者萬五千人。

translations.literal: Rao'an, Dongguang, Anling three counties disaster, burned more than seven thousand households, dead fifteen thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: Rao'an, Dongguang, and Anling suffered a disaster: more than seven thousand households burned, and fifteen thousand people died.

sentences.zh: 後趙寇彭城、下邳，徐州刺史卞敦與征北將軍王邃退保盱眙。

translations.literal: Later Zhao raided Pengcheng and Xiapi; Inspector of Xuzhou Bian Dun and Campaigning-north General Wang Sui withdrew to defend Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao raided Pengcheng and Xiapi; Xuzhou inspector Bian Dun and campaigning-north general Wang Sui withdrew to defend Guangling.

sentences.zh: 敦，壼之從父兄也。

translations.literal: Dun was Bian Chun's paternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was Bian Chun's cousin.

sentences.zh: 王敦謀篡位，諷朝廷征己；

translations.literal: Wang Dun plotted to seize the throne, hinted the court to summon himself;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun plotted to usurp the throne and prompted the court to summon him;

sentences.zh: 帝手詔征之。

translations.literal: The emperor by his own hand edicted to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor issued a personal edict summoning him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，加敦黃鉞、班劍，奏事不名，入朝不趨，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, added Dun golden battle-axe and courtesy swords, when memorializing not using his name, entering court not hurrying, sword and shoes on the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Dun was granted the golden battle-axe and ceremonial swords, permission to memorialize without using his name, to enter court without hurrying, and to wear sword and shoes in the hall.

sentences.zh: 敦移鎮姑孰，屯于湖，以司空導爲司徒，敦自領揚州牧。

translations.literal: Dun shifted his garrison to Gushu, encamped at Yudu, made Minister of Works Dao Minister of Education, Dun himself held Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dun moved his base to Gushu and encamped at Yudu; he made Wang Dao Minister of Education and took the governorship of Yangzhou for himself.

sentences.zh: 敦欲爲逆，王彬諫之甚苦。

translations.literal: Dun wished to rebel; Wang Bin remonstrated very bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun set his heart on rebellion, Wang Bin remonstrated with bitter force.

sentences.zh: 敦變色，目左右，將收之。

translations.literal: Dun's face changed, eyed his attendants, about to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's face darkened; he glanced at his attendants, ready to seize him.

sentences.zh: 彬正色曰：“君昔歲殺兄，今又殺弟邪！

translations.literal: Bin with upright color said: "My lord last year killed an elder brother, now will you kill a younger brother too!
translations.idiomatic: Bin said evenly, "Last year you killed an elder brother—will you kill a younger one now?

sentences.zh: ”敦乃止，以彬爲豫章太守。

translations.literal: " Dun then stopped, made Bin Grand Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: " Dun desisted and made Bin grand administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒遣使結好于慕容廆，廆執送建康。

translations.literal: Later Zhao King Le sent envoys to ally with Murong Hui; Hui seized and sent them to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's king Shi Le sent envoys to court Murong Hui; Hui seized them and sent them on to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 成李驤等進攻寧州，刺史褒中壯公王遜使將軍姚岳等拒之，戰于螗良，成兵大敗。

translations.literal: Cheng's Li Xiang and others advanced on Ning province; Inspector Bao Zhong Duke of Zhuang Wang Sun sent Generals Yao Yue and others to resist; battle at Tangliang, Cheng's army greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang of Cheng advanced on Ning province; inspector Wang Sun, Duke of Zhuang of Baozhong, sent General Yao Yue and others to meet them; at Tangliang the Cheng forces were routed.

sentences.zh: 岳追至瀘水，成兵爭濟，溺死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Yue pursued to the Lu river; Cheng's soldiers scrambling to cross, drowned more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yue pursued to the Lu River; the Cheng troops scrambled to cross, and more than a thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 岳以道遠，不敢濟而還。

translations.literal: Yue because the road was far, did not dare cross and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, finding the road too long, did not dare cross and turned back.

sentences.zh: 遜以岳不窮追，大怒，鞭之，怒甚，冠裂而卒。

translations.literal: Sun because Yue did not pursue to the end, greatly angry, flogged him; rage extreme, cap split and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, furious that Yue had not pursued to the end, flogged him; in his rage his cap burst apart and he died.

sentences.zh: 遜在州十四年，威行殊俗，州人立其子堅行州府事。

translations.literal: Sun was in the province fourteen years, awe extended to foreign lands; the province's people installed his son Jian to handle provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun had ruled the province fourteen years, his authority reaching even foreign peoples; the people installed his son Jian to govern in his stead.

sentences.zh: 詔除堅寧州刺史。

translations.literal: Edict appointed Jian Inspector of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Jian inspector of Ning.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史陶侃遣兵救交州；

translations.literal: Inspector of Guangzhou Tao Kan sent troops to rescue Jiao province;
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou inspector Tao Kan sent troops to relieve Jiao;

sentences.zh: 未至，梁碩拔龍編，奪刺史王諒節，諒不與，碩斷其右臂。

translations.literal: Before arrival, Liang Shuo took Longbian, seized Inspector Wang Liang's staff of authority; Liang would not give it; Shuo cut off his right arm.
translations.idiomatic: before they arrived, Liang Shuo seized Longbian, wrested the inspector's seal from Wang Liang, and when Liang refused, cut off his right arm.

sentences.zh: 諒曰：“死且不避，斷臂何爲！

translations.literal: Liang said: "Facing death I do not flee—what is cutting an arm!
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "I do not shrink from death—what is the loss of an arm?

sentences.zh: ”逾旬而卒。

translations.literal: " After more than ten days, died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: " Within ten days he was dead.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬子，立妃庾氏爲皇后；

translations.literal: Sixth month, renzi, established consort Lady Yu as empress;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renzi, Consort Yu was made empress;

sentences.zh: 以後兄中領軍亮爲中書監。

translations.literal: made the empress's elder brother Central Palace Guard Liang Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and her elder brother Yu Liang, Central Palace Guard, was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 梁碩據交州，凶暴失衆心。

translations.literal: Liang Shuo held Jiao province, fierce and violent lost the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shuo held Jiao, but his cruelty cost him the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 陶侃遣參軍高寶攻碩，斬之。

translations.literal: Tao Kan sent aide Gao Bao to attack Shuo, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan sent his aide Gao Bao against Shuo and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 詔以侃領交州刺史，進號征南大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Edict made Kan hold Inspector of Jiao, advanced title Campaigning-south Grand General, Opening the Government with Honors equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Kan acting inspector of Jiao and advanced him to Campaigning-south Grand General with honors equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 未幾，吏部郎阮放求爲交州刺史，許之。

translations.literal: Before long, Ministry of Personnel Gentleman Ruan Fang sought to be Inspector of Jiao; permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Personnel Gentleman Ruan Fang asked to be made inspector of Jiao, and was granted his request.

sentences.zh: 放行至寧浦，遇高寶，爲寶設饌，伏兵殺之。

translations.literal: Fang traveled to Ningpu, met Gao Bao, set a feast for Bao, hidden troops killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At Ningpu Fang met Gao Bao, entertained him at a feast, and had hidden men kill him.

sentences.zh: 寶兵擊放，放走，得免，至州。

translations.literal: Bao's soldiers attacked Fang; Fang fled, barely escaped, reached the province.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's men attacked Fang; Fang fled, barely escaped with his life, and reached the province.

sentences.zh: 少時，病卒。

translations.literal: Before long, died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 放，鹹之族子也。

translations.literal: Fang, Xian's clansman.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was a clansman of Xian.

sentences.zh: 陳安圍趙征西將軍劉貢于南安，休屠王石武自桑城引兵趣上邽以救之，與貢合擊安，大破之。

translations.literal: Chen An besieged Zhao Western Campaign General Liu Gong at Nan'an; Xiutu king Shi Wu from Sangcheng led troops toward Shanggui to rescue him, with Gong jointly struck An, great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An besieged the Zhao Western Campaign General Liu Gong at Nan'an; the Xiutu king Shi Wu led troops from Sangcheng toward Shanggui to relieve him, joined Gong in attacking An, and routed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 安收餘騎八千，走保隴城。

translations.literal: An gathered remaining horsemen eight thousand, fled to hold Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: An rallied the remaining eight thousand horsemen and fled to hold Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，趙主曜自將圍隴城，別遣兵圍上邽。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Zhao ruler Yao personally led siege of Longcheng, separately dispatched troops to besiege Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Zhao ruler Liu Yao personally led the siege of Longcheng and separately sent troops to besiege Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 安頻出戰，輒敗。

translations.literal: An repeatedly sortied to battle, each time defeated.
translations.idiomatic: An sortied again and again to give battle and was beaten each time.

sentences.zh: 右軍將軍劉幹攻平襄，克之，隴上諸縣悉降。

translations.literal: Right Army General Liu Gan attacked Pingxiang, took it; Longshang all counties entirely submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Army General Liu Gan attacked Pingxiang and took it; all the counties of Longshang submitted.

sentences.zh: 安留其將楊伯支、姜沖兒守隴城，自帥精騎突圍，出奔陝中。

translations.literal: An left his generals Yang Bozhi, Jiang Chong'er to hold Longcheng, himself led picked horsemen to break encirclement, fled out to Shaanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: An left his generals Yang Bozhi and Jiang Chong'er to hold Longcheng, himself led picked horsemen to break through the encirclement, and fled into the mountains of Shaanzhong.

sentences.zh: 曜遣將軍平先等追之。

translations.literal: Yao dispatched General Ping Xian and others to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao dispatched General Ping Xian and others in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 安左揮七尺大刀，右運丈八蛇矛，近則刀矛俱發，輒殪五六人，遠則左右馳射而走。

translations.literal: An left wielded seven-foot great blade, right worked eight-foot serpent spear; close then blade spear both released, each time slew five six men; far then left right galloped shooting and fled.
translations.idiomatic: An swung a seven-foot great blade in his left hand and an eight-foot serpent spear in his right; at close range both weapons struck together and he would slay five or six men at a stroke; at distance he wheeled about shooting left and right as he fled.

sentences.zh: 先亦勇捷如飛，與安搏戰，三交，遂奪其蛇矛。

translations.literal: Xian also brave swift as flight, with An grappled in battle, three exchanges, then seized his serpent spear.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was likewise swift and valiant as flight; he closed with An and fought three bouts, then wrested away his serpent spear.

sentences.zh: 會日暮雨甚，安弃馬與左右匿于山中；

translations.literal: As it happened dusk rain heavy, An abandoned horse with attendants hid in mountains;
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the rain grew torrential; An abandoned his horse and hid in the mountains with his attendants;

sentences.zh: 趙兵索之，不知所在。

translations.literal: Zhao troops searched for him, did not know where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao troops searched for him but could not find where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 明日，安遣其將石容覘趙兵，趙輔威將軍呼延青人獲之，拷問安所在，容卒不肯言，青人殺之。

translations.literal: Next day, An sent his general Shi Rong to spy on Zhao troops; Zhao Assistant Martial Prestige General Huyan Qingren captured him, tortured for where An was; Rong to the end would not speak; Qingren killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day An sent his general Shi Rong to reconnoiter the Zhao army; the Zhao Assistant to the Martial Prestige General Huyan Qingren captured him and tortured him to learn An's whereabouts; Rong would not speak to the end, and Qingren killed him.

sentences.zh: 雨霽，青人尋其迹，獲安于澗曲，斬之。

translations.literal: Rain cleared, Qingren tracked his trail, captured An in ravine bend, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the rain cleared, Qingren followed his trail, seized An in a mountain ravine, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 安善撫將士，與同甘苦，及死，隴上人思之，爲作《壯士之歌》。

translations.literal: An was skilled at cherishing officers and men, shared hardship and ease; when he died, Longshang people missed him, composed for him Song of the Valiant Warrior.
translations.idiomatic: An was skilled at cherishing his officers and men and sharing their hardship and ease; when he died the people of Longshang missed him and composed the "Song of the Valiant Warrior" in his memory.

sentences.zh: 楊伯支斬姜沖兒，以隴城降；

translations.literal: Yang Bozhi beheaded Jiang Chong'er, with Longcheng submitted;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bozhi killed Jiang Chong'er and surrendered Longcheng;

sentences.zh: 別將宋亭斬趙募，以上邽降。

translations.literal: Separate commander Song Ting beheaded Zhao Mu, with Shanggui submitted.
translations.idiomatic: a separate commander, Song Ting, killed Zhao Mu and surrendered Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 曜徙秦州大姓楊、姜諸族二千餘戶于長安。

translations.literal: Yao relocated Qinzhou great clans Yang, Jiang and others more than two thousand households to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao relocated more than two thousand households of the great Yang and Jiang clans of Qinzhou to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 氐、羌皆送任請降；

translations.literal: Di, Qiang all sent hostages requesting submission;
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang all sent hostages to request submission;

sentences.zh: 以赤亭羌酋姚弋仲爲平西將軍，封平襄公。

translations.literal: Appointed Chiting Qiang chief Yao Yizhong as Pacifier of the West general, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed the Chiting Qiang chieftain Yao Yizhong Pacifier of the West General and enfeoffed him as Duke of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 帝畏王敦之逼，欲以郗鑒爲外援，拜鑒兗州刺史，都督揚州江西諸軍事，鎮合肥。

translations.literal: Emperor feared Wang Dun's pressure, wished to use Xi Jian as outside support; appointed Jian Yanzhou governor, commander of Yangzhou west of river military affairs, garrisoned Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared Wang Dun's coercion and wished to use Xi Jian as outside support; he appointed Jian governor of Yanzhou and commander of military affairs south of the Yangzi west of Yangzhou, with his headquarters at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 王敦忌之，表鑒爲尚書令。

translations.literal: Wang Dun resented this, memorialized Jian as Imperial Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun resented this and memorialized to have Jian made Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔征鑒還，道經姑孰，敦與之論西朝人士，曰：“樂彥輔，短才耳。

translations.literal: Eighth month, edict summoned Jian back; passing Gudu, Dun with him discussed Western Court worthies, said: "Le Yifu, shallow talent only.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict summoned Jian back; passing through Gudu, Dun discussed with him the worthies of the Western Court, saying, "Le Yifu is merely a man of shallow talent.

sentences.zh: 考其實，豈勝滿武秋邪！

translations.literal: Judging real merit, how could he surpass Man Wuqiu!
translations.idiomatic: Judging by his real merit, is he truly superior to Man Wuqiu!

sentences.zh: ”鑒曰：“彥輔道韵平淡，湣懷之廢，柔而能正。

translations.literal: " Jian said: "Yifu moral tone level and mild; in Minhuai's removal, gentle yet able to set right.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian said, "Yifu's moral tone is level and mild; in the removal of Emperor Minhuai he was gentle yet able to set things right.

sentences.zh: 武秋失節之士，安得擬之！

translations.literal: Wuqiu is a man who lost integrity—how could he be compared with him!
translations.idiomatic: Wuqiu is a man who lost his integrity—how could he be compared with Yifu!

sentences.zh: ”敦曰：“當是時，危機交急。

translations.literal: " Dun said: "At that time, crises piled upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: " Dun said, "At that time crises piled upon one another.

sentences.zh: ”鑒曰：“丈夫當死生以之。

translations.literal: " Jian said: "A true man should face life and death on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian said, "A true man should face life and death on that basis alone.

sentences.zh: ”敦惡其言，不復相見，久留不遣。

translations.literal: " Dun hated his words, met no more, detained long without releasing.
translations.idiomatic: " Dun hated his words, met with him no more, and detained him long without letting him go.

sentences.zh: 敦黨皆勸敦殺之，敦不從。

translations.literal: Dun's faction all urged Dun to kill him; Dun did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's faction all urged Dun to kill him, but Dun would not consent.

sentences.zh: 鑒還台，遂與帝謀討敦。

translations.literal: Jian returned to capital, thereupon with emperor plotted to campaign against Dun.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian returned to the capital, he thereupon plotted with the emperor to campaign against Dun.

sentences.zh: 後趙中山公虎帥步騎四萬擊安東將軍曹嶷，青州郡縣多降之，遂圍廣固。

translations.literal: Later Zhao Prince of Zhongshan Hu led foot horse forty thousand to attack Eastern Pacification General Cao Ni; Qingzhou prefectures counties largely submitted; then besieged Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's Prince of Zhongshan, Shi Hu, led forty thousand foot and horse to attack the Eastern Pacification General Cao Ni; most of Qingzhou's prefectures and counties submitted, and he then besieged Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 嶷出降，送襄國殺之，坑其衆三萬。

translations.literal: Ni came out and submitted; sent to Xiangguo and executed; buried alive his followers thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ni came out and surrendered; they sent him to Xiangguo and executed him, and buried alive thirty thousand of his followers.

sentences.zh: 虎欲盡殺嶷衆，青州刺史劉征曰：“今留征，使牧民也，無民焉牧！

translations.literal: Hu wished to kill all of Ni's people; Qingzhou governor Liu Zheng said: "Now you keep Zheng to shepherd the people—without people, whom shall I shepherd!
translations.idiomatic: Hu wished to kill all of Ni's followers; the Qingzhou governor Liu Zheng said, "You have kept me here to shepherd the people—without people, whom shall I shepherd!

sentences.zh: 征將歸耳！

translations.literal: Zheng is going home!
translations.idiomatic: I am going home!

sentences.zh: ”虎乃留男女七百口配征，使鎮廣固。

translations.literal: " Hu then left male female seven hundred persons to accompany Zheng, made him garrison Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu then left seven hundred men and women to accompany Zheng and stationed him to hold Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜自隴上西擊凉州，遣其將劉咸攻韓璞于冀城，呼延晏攻寧羌護軍陰鑒于桑壁，曜自將戎卒二十八萬軍于河上，列營百餘裏，金鼓之聲動地，河水爲沸，張茂臨河諸戍，皆望風奔潰。

translations.literal: Zhao ruler Yao from Longshang west attacked Liangzhou; dispatched his generals Liu Xian to attack Han Pu at Jicheng, Huyan Yan to attack Ningqiang Protector of the Army Yin Jian at Sangbi; Yao personally led barbarian soldiers two hundred eighty thousand encamped on the river, camps lined more than hundred li; drums and gongs shook the earth, river water seemed to boil; Zhang Mao's river garrisons all at sight of wind fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao ruler Liu Yao marched west from Longshang to attack Liangzhou; he sent his general Liu Xian to attack Han Pu at Jicheng and Huyan Yan to attack the Ningqiang Protector of the Army Yin Jian at Sangbi; Yao personally led an army of two hundred eighty thousand tribal soldiers and encamped along the river, his camps stretching more than a hundred li; the thunder of drums and gongs shook the earth and the river seemed to boil; every garrison of Zhang Mao along the river fled at the mere sight of his banners.

sentences.zh: 曜揚聲欲百道俱濟，直抵姑臧，凉州大震。

translations.literal: Yao proclaimed intent to cross by a hundred routes at once, strike straight to Guzang; Liangzhou greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Yao proclaimed that he would cross at a hundred points at once and march straight on Guzang; all Liangzhou was shaken.

sentences.zh: 參軍馬岌勸茂親出拒戰，長史汜禕怒，請斬之。

translations.literal: Staff officer Ma Ji urged Mao personally to go out and resist in battle; Chief Administrator Si Yi in anger requested to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The staff officer Ma Ji urged Mao to go out in person and give battle; the chief administrator Si Yi in anger asked that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 岌曰：“汜公糟粕書生，刺舉小才，不思家國大計。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Lord Si is a dregs-and-lees bookish man, a petty talent for impeachment, who does not ponder the great design of state and family.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Lord Si is a bookish mediocrity, a petty talent for impeachment who gives no thought to the great design of state and family.

sentences.zh: 明公父子欲爲朝廷誅劉曜有年矣，今曜自至，遠近之情，共觀明公此舉，當立信勇之驗以副秦、隴之望。

translations.literal: Your lordship father and son wished for the court to execute Liu Yao these many years; now Yao has come himself; near and far all watch your lordship's move this time—you should establish proof of trust and courage to answer Qin and Long's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Your lordship and your father have for years wished to execute Liu Yao on the court's behalf; now Yao has come in person, and men near and far alike watch what you will do—you must prove your trust and courage and answer the hopes of Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 力雖不敵，勢不可以不出。

translations.literal: Strength though not equal, the situation cannot permit not going out.
translations.idiomatic: Though our strength is unequal, the situation cannot permit us to stay within.

sentences.zh: ”茂曰：“善！

translations.literal: " Mao said: "Good!
translations.idiomatic: " Mao said, "Well said!

sentences.zh: ”乃出屯石頭。

translations.literal: " He then went out and encamped at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went out and encamped at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 茂謂參軍陳珍曰：“劉曜舉三秦之衆，乘勝席捲而來，將若之何？

translations.literal: Mao said to staff officer Chen Zhen: "Liu Yao has raised the hosts of the Three Qins and comes sweeping on the tide of victory—what shall we do?
translations.idiomatic: Mao said to the staff officer Chen Zhen, "Liu Yao has raised the hosts of the Three Qins and comes sweeping on the tide of victory—what are we to do?

sentences.zh: ”珍曰：“曜兵雖多，精卒至少，大抵皆氐、羌烏合之衆，恩信未洽，且有山東之虞，安能舍其腹心之疾，曠日持久，與我爭河西之地邪！

translations.literal: " Zhen said: "Yao's troops though many, picked soldiers are few; for the most part they are Di and Qiang rabble gathered together, favor and trust not yet harmonized, and moreover he has worries east of the mountains—how could he abandon his heartland's ills, prolong days and months, and with us contest the lands west of the river!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen said, "Though Yao's army is large, his picked troops are few; for the most part they are a rabble of Di and Qiang, their loyalty not yet won, and he has troubles east of the mountains as well—how could he abandon the troubles at his heart, linger for months, and contest the Hexi with us!

sentences.zh: 若二旬不退，珍請得弊卒數千，爲明公擒之。

translations.literal: If within twenty days he does not withdraw, Zhen requests a few thousand worn troops to capture him for your lordship.
translations.idiomatic: If he does not withdraw within twenty days, I ask only a few thousand worn troops and I will capture him for your lordship.

sentences.zh: ”茂喜，使珍將兵救韓璞。

translations.literal: " Mao was pleased and sent Zhen to lead troops to rescue Han Pu.
translations.idiomatic: " Mao was pleased and sent Zhen to lead troops to relieve Han Pu.

sentences.zh: 趙諸將爭欲濟河，趙主曜曰：“吾軍勢雖盛，然畏威而來者三分有二，中軍疲困，其實難用。

translations.literal: Zhao generals all vied to cross the river; Zhao ruler Yao said: "Our army's force though grand, yet those who came from fear of our might are two parts in three; the central army is weary and spent—in truth hard to use.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao generals all clamored to cross the river; the Zhao ruler Liu Yao said, "Though our army looks mighty, two thirds of it came only from fear of our might; the central force is weary and spent and in truth hard to use.

sentences.zh: 今但按甲勿動，以吾威聲震之，若出中旬張茂之表不至者，吾爲負卿矣。

translations.literal: Now only hold armor and do not move; with our martial renown shake them—if past mid-month Zhang Mao's submission does not arrive, I have failed you.
translations.idiomatic: For now hold the army still and let our martial renown shake them—if past mid-month Zhang Mao's letter of submission has not arrived, I have failed you.

sentences.zh: ”茂尋遣使稱籓，獻馬、牛、羊、珍寶不可勝紀。

translations.literal: " Before long Mao sent envoys to declare himself a vassal, presenting horses, cattle, sheep, treasures beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Mao sent envoys to declare himself a vassal and presented horses, cattle, sheep, and treasures beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 曜拜茂侍中、都督凉、南北秦、梁、益、巴、漢、隴右、西域雜夷、匈奴諸軍事、太師、凉州牧，封凉王，加九錫。

translations.literal: Yao appointed Mao Palace Attendant, commander of Liang, North and South Qin, Liang, Yi, Ba, Han, Longyou, Western Regions mixed barbarians, Xiongnu military affairs, Grand Preceptor, Liangzhou governor; enfeoffed as King of Liang; added Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Yao appointed Mao Palace Attendant and commander of military affairs for Liang, North and South Qin, Liang, Yi, Ba, Han, Longyou, the mixed peoples of the Western Regions, and the Xiongnu; made him Grand Preceptor and governor of Liangzhou; enfeoffed him as King of Liang; and granted him the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 楊難敵聞陳安死，大懼，與弟堅頭南奔漢中，趙鎮西將軍劉厚追擊之，大獲而還。

translations.literal: Yang Nandi heard Chen An had died, greatly feared; with his brother Jiantou fled south to Hanzhong; Zhao Pacifier of the West General Liu Hou pursued and struck them, great booty and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandi, hearing that Chen An was dead, was greatly afraid; he and his brother Jiantou fled south into Hanzhong; the Zhao Pacifier of the West General Liu Hou pursued them, took a rich spoil, and returned.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜以大鴻臚田崧爲鎮南大將軍、益州刺史，鎮仇池。

translations.literal: Zhao ruler Yao appointed Grand Herald Tian Song as Pacifier of the South Grand General and Yizhou governor, garrisoned Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao ruler Liu Yao appointed the Grand Herald Tian Song Pacifier of the South Grand General and governor of Yizhou, with his headquarters at Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 難敵送任請降于成，成安北將軍李稚受難敵賂，不送難敵于成都。

translations.literal: Nandi sent hostages requesting submission to Cheng; Cheng's Pacifier of the North General Li Zhi accepted Nandi's bribe and did not send Nandi to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Nandi sent hostages to request submission to Cheng; Cheng's Pacifier of the North General Li Zhi took Nandi's bribe and did not send him on to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 趙兵退，即遣不武都，難敵遂據險不服。

translations.literal: When Zhao troops withdrew, he at once sent troops not to Wudu; Nandi then held the passes and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhao army withdrew, he at once sent troops away from Wudu; Nandi then held the mountain passes and refused submission.

sentences.zh: 稚自悔失計，亟請討之。

translations.literal: Zhi himself regretted his miscalculation and urgently requested a campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi himself regretted his blunder and urgently asked to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 雄遣稚兄侍中、中領軍琀與稚出白水，征東將軍李壽及琀弟玝出陰平，以擊難敵；

translations.literal: Xiong dispatched Zhi's elder brother Palace Attendant, Central Army Commander Huan with Zhi out by Baishui; Eastern Campaign General Li Shou and Huan's younger brother Yu out by Yinping, to strike Nandi;
translations.idiomatic: Xiong sent Zhi's elder brother, the Palace Attendant and Central Army Commander Li Huan, with Zhi out by Baishui, and the Eastern Campaign General Li Shou with Huan's younger brother Li Yu out by Yinping, to attack Nandi;

sentences.zh: 群臣諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Ministers remonstrated; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers remonstrated, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 難敵遣兵拒之，壽、玝不得進，而琀、稚長驅至下辨。

translations.literal: Nandi dispatched troops to resist them; Shou and Yu could not advance, while Huan and Zhi drove straight through to Xiabian.
translations.idiomatic: Nandi sent troops to resist them; Shou and Yu could not advance, while Huan and Zhi drove straight through to Xiabian.

sentences.zh: 難敵遣兵斷其歸路，四面攻之。

translations.literal: Nandi dispatched troops to cut off their line of retreat and attacked from four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Nandi sent troops to cut off their line of retreat and attacked from every side.

sentences.zh: 琀、稚深入無繼，皆爲難敵所殺，死者數千人。

translations.literal: Huan and Zhi had penetrated deep without support; both were killed by Nandi; the dead numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Huan and Zhi had penetrated deep without support; both were killed by Nandi, and several thousand men died with them.

sentences.zh: 琀，蕩之長子，有才望，雄欲以爲嗣，聞其死，不食者數日。

translations.literal: Huan was Dang's eldest son, had talent and reputation; Xiong wished to make him heir; hearing of his death, went without food for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was the eldest son of Li Dang, a man of talent and reputation whom Xiong had wished to make his heir; hearing of his death, Xiong ate nothing for several days.

sentences.zh: 初，趙主曜長子儉，次子胤。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhao ruler Yao's eldest son was Jian, second son Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Zhao ruler Liu Yao's eldest son was Liu Jian and his second son was Liu Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤年十歲，長七尺五寸，漢主聰奇之，謂曜曰：“此兒神氣，非義真之比也，當以爲嗣。

translations.literal: Yin at age ten was seven feet five inches tall; Han ruler Cong marveled at him and said to Yao: "This boy's spirit is not comparable to Yizhen's—he should be made heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was ten years old he stood seven feet five inches tall; the Han ruler Liu Cong marveled at him and said to Yao, "This boy's spirit is not to be compared with Yizhen's—he should be made your heir.

sentences.zh: ”曜曰：“籓國之嗣，能守祭祀足矣，不敢亂長幼之序。

translations.literal: " Yao said: "Heir of a feudatory state need only keep the sacrifices—that is enough; I dare not disturb the order of elder and younger.
translations.idiomatic: " Yao said, "The heir of a feudatory state need only keep the sacrifices—that is enough; I dare not disturb the order of elder and younger.

sentences.zh: ”聰曰：“卿之勛德，當世受專征之任，非他臣之比也，吾當更以一國封義真。

translations.literal: " Cong said: "Your lordship's merit and virtue in this age bear the charge of independent campaigning—not comparable with other ministers; I shall enfeoff Yizhen with another state besides.
translations.idiomatic: " Cong said, "Your merit and virtue in this age bear the charge of independent campaigning—you are not comparable with other ministers; I shall enfeoff Yizhen with another state besides.

sentences.zh: ”乃封儉爲臨海王，立胤爲世子。

translations.literal: " He then enfeoffed Jian as Prince of Linhai and established Yin as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " He then enfeoffed Jian as Prince of Linhai and established Yin as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 既長，多力善射，驍捷如風。

translations.literal: When he had grown, great strength and skill in archery, bold and swift as wind.
translations.idiomatic: When he had grown to manhood he was immensely strong and skilled in archery, bold and swift as the wind.

sentences.zh: 靳准之亂，沒于黑匿郁鞠部。

translations.literal: In Jin Zhun's rebellion he was lost among the Heiyu Yuju tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Zhun's rebellion he was lost among the Heiyu Yuju tribe.

sentences.zh: 陳安既敗，胤自言于郁鞠，郁鞠大驚，禮而歸之。

translations.literal: After Chen An was defeated, Yin presented himself to Yuju; Yuju was greatly startled, treated him with ceremony and returned him.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen An's defeat, Yin presented himself to Yuju; Yuju was greatly startled, received him with full ceremony, and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 曜悲喜，謂君臣曰：“義光雖已爲太子，然沖幼儒謹，恐不堪今之多難。

translations.literal: Yao was both glad and sorrowful and said to his ministers: "Yiguang though already made crown prince is yet young, studious, and cautious—I fear he cannot bear today's many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was both glad and sorrowful and said to his ministers, "Though Yiguang is already crown prince, he is still young, studious, and cautious—I fear he cannot bear today's many hardships.

sentences.zh: 義孫，故世子也，材器過人，且涉曆艱難。

translations.literal: Yisun, the former heir apparent, talent and capacity surpass others, and moreover has passed through hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun, the former heir apparent, surpasses others in talent and capacity and has moreover passed through hardship.

sentences.zh: 吾欲法周文王、漢光武，以固社稷而安義光，何如？

translations.literal: I wish to follow King Wen of Zhou and Emperor Guangwu of Han, to secure the altars of state and settle Yiguang—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I wish to follow King Wen of Zhou and Emperor Guangwu of Han, to secure the altars of state and settle Yiguang in safety—what do you think?

sentences.zh: ”太傅呼延晏等皆曰：“陛下爲國家無窮之計，豈惟臣等賴之，實宗廟四海之慶。

translations.literal: " Grand Tutor Huyan Yan and others all said: "Your Majesty plans for the state's boundless future—not only do we ministers rely on it; it is truly a rejoicing for the ancestral temples and all within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand Tutor Huyan Yan and the others all said, "Your Majesty's plan looks to the state's boundless future—not only do we your ministers rely on it; it is truly a rejoicing for the ancestral temples and all within the four seas.

sentences.zh: ”左光祿大夫卜泰、太子太保韓廣進曰：“陛下以廢立爲是，不應更問群臣；

translations.literal: " Left Honored Grandee Bu Tai and Heir Apparent Grand Guardian Han Guang advanced and said: "If Your Majesty holds deposition and establishment right, you should not again ask the ministers;
translations.idiomatic: " The Left Honored Grandee Bu Tai and the Heir Apparent's Grand Guardian Han Guang stepped forward and said, "If Your Majesty is sure that deposition and establishment are right, you should not again ask your ministers;

sentences.zh: 若以爲疑，固樂聞异同之言。

translations.literal: if you hold it in doubt, we are indeed glad to hear differing views.
translations.idiomatic: if you are in doubt, we are indeed glad to hear differing views.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以爲廢太子，非也。

translations.literal: Your servant privately holds that deposing the crown prince is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately holds that deposing the crown prince is wrong.

sentences.zh: 昔文王定嗣于未立之前，則可也；

translations.literal: In old times King Wen fixed the succession before any heir was established—that could be done;
translations.idiomatic: In old times King Wen fixed the succession before any heir had been established—that could be done;

sentences.zh: 光武以母失恩而廢其子，豈足爲聖朝之法！

translations.literal: Guangwu because the mother lost favor deposed her son—how could that suffice as law for a sagely court!
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu deposed his son because the mother had lost favor—how could that suffice as a precedent for a sagely court!

sentences.zh: 向以東海爲嗣，未必不如明帝也。

translations.literal: Formerly making the Prince of Donghai heir was not necessarily inferior to Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Making the Prince of Donghai heir was not necessarily inferior to Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 胤文武才略，誠高絕于世。

translations.literal: Yin's civil and military talent and stratagem truly tower above the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's civil and military talent and stratagem truly tower above the age.

sentences.zh: 然太子孝友仁慈，亦足爲承平賢主。

translations.literal: Yet the crown prince is filial, friendly, and benevolent—he too suffices as a worthy ruler in peaceful times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the crown prince is filial, friendly, and benevolent—he too would suffice as a worthy ruler in peaceful times.

sentences.zh: 况東宮者，民、神所系，豈可輕動！

translations.literal: Moreover the Eastern Palace is what the people and spirits depend on—how could it be lightly moved!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Eastern Palace is what the people and the spirits depend on—how could it be lightly moved!

sentences.zh: 陛下誠欲如是，臣等有死而已，不敢奉詔，”曜默然。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes this, your servants have only death—we dare not obey the decree," Yao was silent.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes this, we your servants have only death to offer—we dare not obey such a decree." Yao was silent.

sentences.zh: 胤進曰：“父之于子，當愛之如一，今黜熙而立臣，臣何敢自安！

translations.literal: Yin advanced and said: "A father toward sons should love them as one; now deposing Xi and establishing me—how dare I be at ease!
translations.idiomatic: Yin stepped forward and said, "A father toward his sons should love them as one; now to depose Xi and establish me—how dare I be at ease!

sentences.zh: 陛下苟以臣爲頗堪驅策，豈不能輔熙以承聖業乎！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty holds me somewhat fit to be driven, could I not assist Xi in undertaking the sagely enterprise!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty holds me somewhat fit to serve, could I not assist Xi in undertaking the sagely enterprise!

sentences.zh: 必若以臣代熙，臣請效死于此，不敢聞命。

translations.literal: If you must use me to replace Xi, I beg to offer my death here—I dare not hear the command.
translations.idiomatic: If you must use me to replace Xi, I beg to die here rather than hear such a command.

sentences.zh: ”因歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: " He then sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sobbed and wept.

sentences.zh: 曜亦以熙羊後所生，不忍廢也，乃追謚前妃卜氏爲元悼皇后。

translations.literal: Yao also because Xi was born after the sheep year, could not bear to depose him; he then posthumously titled former consort the Bu clan as Primary Lamenting Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Yao also, because Xi had been born after the year of the sheep, could not bear to depose him; he then posthumously titled his former consort of the Bu clan Primary Lamenting Empress.

sentences.zh: 泰，即胤之舅也，曜喜其公忠，以爲上光祿大夫、儀同三司、領太子太傅；

translations.literal: Tai was Yin's maternal uncle; Yao delighted in his public loyalty and made him Superior Honored Grandee, equal to the Three Excellencies, and concurrently Heir Apparent Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Tai was Yin's maternal uncle; Yao delighted in his public loyalty and made him Superior Honored Grandee with the privileges of the Three Excellencies and concurrently Heir Apparent's Grand Tutor;

sentences.zh: 封胤爲永安王，拜侍中、衛大將軍、都督二宮禁衛諸軍事、開府儀同三司、錄尚書事，命熙于胤盡家人之禮。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed Yin as Prince of Yong'an; appointed Palace Attendant, Guard Grand General, commander of the two palaces' inner guard military affairs, opened office equal to Three Excellencies, recorded Secretariat affairs; ordered Xi toward Yin to observe full family courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Yin as Prince of Yong'an, appointed him Palace Attendant, Guard Grand General, commander of the two palaces' inner-guard military affairs, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies and charge of recording Secretariat affairs, and ordered Xi to observe full family courtesy toward Yin.

sentences.zh: 張茂大城姑臧，修靈鈞台。

translations.literal: Zhang Mao greatly walled Guzang and restored the Lingjun Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao greatly fortified Guzang and restored the Lingjun Terrace.

sentences.zh: 別駕吳紹諫曰：“明公所以修城築台者，蓋懲既往之患耳。

translations.literal: Assistant Governor Wu Shao remonstrated: "Your lordship's reason for repairing walls and building terraces is surely to take warning from past troubles.
translations.idiomatic: The Assistant Governor Wu Shao remonstrated, "Your lordship repairs walls and builds terraces surely to take warning from past troubles.

sentences.zh: 愚以爲苟恩未洽于人心，雖處層台，亦無所益，適足以疑群下忠信之志，失士民系托之望，示怯弱之形，啓鄰敵之謀，將何以佐天子、霸諸候乎！

translations.literal: I foolishly hold that if favor has not yet harmonized in men's hearts, though you dwell on lofty terraces there is no benefit; it only suffices to make the loyal faith of the host doubt, lose scholars and commoners' hopes of relying on you, show a timid weak form, and open neighboring enemies' schemes—how will you assist the Son of Heaven and hegemon over the feudal lords!
translations.idiomatic: I hold that if your grace has not yet won men's hearts, dwelling on lofty terraces will do no good; it will only make your followers doubt your loyal intent, lose the hopes scholars and commoners place in you, show a timid weakness, and invite neighboring enemies' designs—how then will you assist the Son of Heaven and hegemon over the feudal lords!

sentences.zh: 願亟罷茲役，以息勞費。

translations.literal: I wish you would quickly halt this labor to rest toil and expense.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to halt this work at once and spare the people's toil and expense.

sentences.zh: ”茂曰：“亡兄一旦失身于物，豈無忠臣義士欲盡節者哉！

translations.literal: " Mao said: "My late elder brother in a single day lost his person to circumstance—were there not loyal ministers and righteous men who wished to exhaust their integrity!
translations.idiomatic: " Mao said, "My late elder brother in a single day lost his life to circumstance—were there not loyal ministers and righteous men who wished to give their all!

sentences.zh: 顧禍生不意，雖有智勇，無所施耳。

translations.literal: Only disaster arose unlooked-for; though they had wisdom and courage, there was nowhere to apply it.
translations.idiomatic: Only disaster arose unlooked-for; though they had wisdom and courage, there was nowhere to apply it.

sentences.zh: 王公設險，勇夫重閉，古之道也。

translations.literal: Kings and dukes set defenses; brave men double the gates—this is the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: Kings and dukes set defenses; brave men double the gates—that is the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 今國家未靖，不可以太平之理責人于屯邅之世也。

translations.literal: Now the state is not yet settled—you cannot with the logic of peace demand of men in an age of hardship and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is not yet settled; one cannot judge men in an age of hardship and obstruction by the standards of peace.

sentences.zh: ”卒爲之。

translations.literal: " In the end he completed it.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he went ahead with the work.

sentences.zh: 王敦從子允之，方總角，敦愛其聰警，常以自隨。

translations.literal: Wang Dun's nephew by a collateral line, Yunzhi, was just at the age of the hair-knot; Dun loved his clever alertness and often kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's young nephew Yunzhi was still a boy; Dun doted on his quick wit and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 敦常夜飲，允之辭醉先臥。

translations.literal: Dun often drank at night; Yunzhi pleaded drunkenness and went to bed first.
translations.idiomatic: Dun often drank late into the night; Yunzhi would plead drunkenness and retire to bed first.

sentences.zh: 敦與錢鳳謀爲逆，允之悉聞其言。

translations.literal: Dun and Qian Feng plotted rebellion; Yunzhi heard all their words.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun and Qian Feng plotted rebellion, Yunzhi overheard every word.

sentences.zh: 即于臥處大吐，衣面幷污。

translations.literal: He at once vomited heavily where he lay, soiling both clothes and face.
translations.idiomatic: He promptly vomited all over his bedding, fouling his clothes and face.

sentences.zh: 鳳出，敦果照視，見允之臥于吐中，不復疑之。

translations.literal: Feng went out; Dun indeed came with a lamp to look and saw Yunzhi lying amid the vomit, and no longer suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng left, Dun came with a lamp to check and found Yunzhi sprawled in the vomit; he suspected him no more.

sentences.zh: 會其父舒拜廷尉，允之求歸省父，悉以敦、鳳之謀白舒。

translations.literal: It happened that his father Shu was appointed Minister of Justice; Yunzhi asked to return home to visit his father and told Shu in full the plot of Dun and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Shu was appointed Minister of Justice, Yunzhi asked leave to visit him and revealed the whole plot of Dun and Feng.

sentences.zh: 舒與王導俱啓帝，陰爲之備。

translations.literal: Shu and Wang Dao together informed the emperor and secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Wang Dao jointly informed the emperor and quietly prepared their defenses.

sentences.zh: 敦欲强其宗族，陵弱帝室，冬，十一月，徙王含爲征東將軍、都督揚州江西諸軍事，王舒爲荊州刺史、監荊州沔南諸軍事，王彬爲江州刺史。

translations.literal: Dun wished to strengthen his clan and overwhelm the imperial house; in winter, the eleventh month, he transferred Wang Han to Eastern Campaigning General and commander of all military affairs west of the Yangzhou line, Wang Shu to governor of Jing Province and overseer of military affairs south of the Mian in Jing, and Wang Bin to governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to strengthen his clan and dominate the throne, Wang Dun in the eleventh month of winter transferred Wang Han to command forces west of the Yangzhou line, Wang Shu to Jing Province, and Wang Bin to Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒以參軍樊坦爲章武內史，勒見其衣冠弊壞，問之。

translations.literal: Later Zhao King Le made his staff officer Fan Tan internal administrator of Zhangwu; when Le saw his cap and robes worn and ruined, he asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's King Le appointed his aide Fan Tan internal administrator of Zhangwu; seeing Fan's clothes in tatters, Le asked why.

sentences.zh: 坦率然對曰：“傾爲羯賊所掠，資財蕩盡。

translations.literal: Tan answered frankly and plainly: "I was lately plundered by the Jie bandits, and my property was swept away entirely."
translations.idiomatic: Fan answered bluntly, "I was just robbed by the Jie raiders and lost everything I had."

sentences.zh: ”勒笑曰：“羯賊乃爾無道邪！

translations.literal: " Le laughed and said, "The Jie bandits are thus lawless!"
translations.idiomatic: " Le laughed and said, "So the Jie are that lawless!"

sentences.zh: 今當相償。

translations.literal: Now I shall make restitution to you.
translations.idiomatic: I shall make it up to you now.

sentences.zh: ”坦大懼，叩頭泣謝。

translations.literal: " Tan was greatly afraid and kowtowed, weeping in apology.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan was terrified and kowtowed, weeping his apologies.

sentences.zh: 勒賜車馬、衣服、裝錢三百萬而遣之。

translations.literal: Le bestowed carriages and horses, clothing, and three million in travel money and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Le gave him carriages, horses, clothing, and three million in travel funds and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 是歲，越巂斯叟攻成將任回，成主雄遣征南將軍費黑討之。

translations.literal: That year, the Suo of Yuexi attacked Cheng general Ren Hui; Cheng ruler Xiong sent Southern Campaigning General Fei Hei to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Suo of Yuexi attacked the Cheng general Ren Hui; the Cheng ruler Xiong sent the Southern Campaigning General Fei Hei against them.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史周札，一門五候，宗族强盛，吳士莫與爲比，王敦忌之。

translations.literal: Zhou Zha, internal administrator of Kuaiji, had five marquises in one household; his clan was powerful, and no Wu gentleman could be compared with him—Wang Dun resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zha of Kuaiji had five marquises in a single family; his clan was mighty beyond any in Wu, and Wang Dun envied him.

sentences.zh: 敦有疾，錢鳳勸敦早除周氏，敦然之。

translations.literal: Dun fell ill; Qian Feng urged Dun to eliminate the Zhou clan early, and Dun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun fell ill, Qian Feng urged him to destroy the Zhou clan at once, and Dun agreed.

sentences.zh: 周嵩以兄顗之死，心常憤憤。

translations.literal: Zhou Song, because of his elder brother Yi's death, constantly harbored anger in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Song, grieving his brother Yi's death, nursed a constant rage.

sentences.zh: 敦無子，養王含之子應爲嗣，嵩嘗于衆中言應不宜統兵，敦惡之。

translations.literal: Dun had no son and adopted Wang Han's son Ying as heir; Song once said in the assembly that Ying was unfit to command troops, and Dun hated him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Dun had no son and adopted Wang Han's son Ying as his heir; Song once declared in public that Ying was unfit to command troops, and Dun took offense.

sentences.zh: 嵩與札兄子莛皆爲敦從事中郎。

translations.literal: Song and Zha's elder brother's son Ting both served Dun as attendants-in-service.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Zha's nephew Ting both served as Wang Dun's attendants.

sentences.zh: 會道士李脫以妖術惑衆，士民頗信事之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Daoist Li Tuo used demonic arts to delude the masses, and scholars and commoners largely trusted and served him.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist named Li Tuo used sorcery to mislead the people, and many gentry and commoners followed him.
